<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro_main}
The Laplace transforms of the measures \(\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}_{N,T}\) converge as \(N,T\to\infty\).
In particular, $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}_{T,N}$ converges weakly to a probability measure $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}$ on $\Omega^1 \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{T}^2)\times \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{T}^2)$. Furthermore, the gauge marginal of $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu^{{\mathrm{A}}}$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
Let $\kappa>0$ and $n$ be the degree of the polynomial $\mathcal{V}$ defined in \eqref{eq:def_V}. There exists $\eta_{\mathrm{A}},\eta_\Phi>0$ such that
    \[
    \mathbb{E}_{\mu^{\mathrm{YMH}}}[e^{\eta_{\mathrm{A}}\|A\|_{C^{-\kappa}}^2+ \eta_\Phi \|\phi\|_{C^{-\kappa}}^{2n}}]<\infty.
    \]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:gauge_covariance}
    The measure $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}[g]}_{N,T}$ converges (in the same sense as $\mu^{\mathrm{YMH}}_{N,T}$) as $N,T\to\infty$. Furthermore, for any continuous and bounded function $F$ on $\Omega^1\mathcal{S}'\times \mathcal{S}'$
    \[
    \int F(A,\phi)\,\mathrm{d} \mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}[g]}(A,\phi)=\int F(A^g,\phi^g) \,\mathrm{d}\mu^{\mathrm{YMH}}(A,\phi).
    \]
  In particular, $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}[g]}=\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}$ on gauge-invariant observables, i.e. whenever $F$ satisfies $F(A,\phi)=F(A^g,\phi^g)$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Proposition~\ref{prop:coulomb_representative} gives the gauge-fixing statement for $H^1$ configurations. The corresponding formal integral calculation is given in Appendix~\ref{app:gauge_fixing}, see \eqref{eq:formal_computation_gauge_change}.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:linear_covariant_gauges}
The measure $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}(\alpha)}_{N,T}$ has a unique limit as $N,T\to\infty$ to a probability measure denoted by $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}(\alpha)}$. In fact, one has for any bounded continuous function $F$ on $\Omega^1\mathcal{S}'\times \mathcal{S}'$
\[
\int F(A,\phi)\,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}(\alpha)}(A,\phi)=\int F(A^{{\mathscr g}^{\alpha^{-1/2}\zeta}}, \phi^{{\mathscr g}^{\alpha^{-1/2}\zeta}})  \,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi)  \,\mathrm{d}\nu(\zeta).
\]
In particular, the measures coincide on gauge-invariant observables. Finally,
\[
\lim_{\alpha\to \infty} \int F(A,\phi)\,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}(\alpha)}(A,\phi)= \int F(A,\phi)  \,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi) .
\]
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
Formally, our Colomb gauge construction from Theorem~\ref{thm:intro_main} can be obtained $\alpha=\infty$ in the action~\eqref{eq:YMH_action_alpha} for the formal measure in consideration. In fact, the previous theorem makes that rigorous.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:large_deviations}
    The measures $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}};\varepsilon}$ satisfy a Laplace principle principle for every bounded, Lipschitz and gauge invariant function $f=f(A,\phi)$. More precisely
    \begin{align*}
    &-\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \varepsilon\log \int \exp(-\varepsilon^{-1}f(A,\phi))\,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}};\varepsilon}\\  =& \inf_{(A,\phi)\in\Omega^1 H^1\times H^1}
\bigl\{f(A,\phi)+\mathcal{S}_{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi)\bigr\}
-\inf_{(A,\phi)\in\Omega^1 H^1\times H^1}
\mathcal{S}_{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi).\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical}
Let $B\in\Omega^1H^1$,
and $s\in \mathbb{R}$. For any $\mathfrak{Re}(z)>0$ such that $|z|\geq 1$ and $\eta\in [0,2]$,  we have
\[
\|R_B(z)f\|_{H^s_B}\lesssim |z|^{\frac\eta 2-1}\|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
This is standard as we are working on the ``{intrinsic}'' Sobolev spaces (alternatively,  one can prove it with functional calculus).
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:semi-group}
    For any $\lambda>0$ and any $B\in \Omega^1L^{2}$ taking values in $i \mathbb{R}$ almost everywhere, the operator $(L_B+\lambda)$ is self-adjoint, positive-definite, and generates a strongly continuous semigroup. The resolvent of $L_B$ has the following $L^{2}$-kernel representation and, for any $\gamma>0$, fractional-power operator representation:
    \begin{align*}
    R_B(\lambda)(x,y) &= \int_0^\infty\; e^{-\lambda t}p_B(t,x,y)\,\mathrm{d} t, \\
    R_B (\lambda)^\gamma &= \frac{1}{\Gamma(\gamma)}\int_0^\infty\; t^{\gamma -1} e^{-\lambda t} p_B(t)\,\mathrm{d} t.
    \end{align*}
    Here $\Gamma$ is the usual Gamma function. The second identity holds for the kernels as well.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:diamagnetic}
Let $B \in \Omega^1 H^1$ with $B$ taking values in ${\mathbf i} \mathbb{R}$ almost everywhere. Then, for all $t > 0$, $\lambda>0$, $\gamma>0$ and almost every $(x,y)\in\mathbb{T}^2 \times \mathbb{T}^2$,
    \[
    |p_B(t,x,y)| \le p_0(t,x-y), \qquad
    |R_B(\lambda)^\gamma(x,y)| \le R_0(\lambda)^\gamma(x-y).
    \]
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We first recall the Feynman-Kac representation for smooth $B\in\Omega^1C^\infty$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:FK}
p_B(t,x,y) = p_0(t,x,y) \mathbf{E}_{t;y\to x}\Big[\exp\Big(-\int_0^t\; B^*(W_s) \,\mathrm{d} W_s -\int_0^t\; \mathrm{d}^* B(W_s) \,\mathrm{d} s\Big)\Big]\;,
\end{equation}
where $W$ is a Brownian bridge under which the expectation $\mathbf{E}_{t;y\to x}$ goes from $y$ to $x$ on the time interval $[0,t]$.
Note that the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:FK} is defined for every $t>0$ and $x,y\in\mathbb{T}^{2}$ (and is unchanged if $B$ is changed on a null set), while for  $B\in \Omega^1H^1$ the left-hand side is an integral kernel and hence only defined up to null sets; \eqref{eq:FK} asserts that the former is a representative of the latter. For continuous $B$ and $\mathrm{d}^{*}B$, \eqref{eq:FK} holds pointwise for all $x,y$, and the general case follows by taking $B_{\varepsilon}\in\Omega^1C^{\infty}$ with $B_{\varepsilon}\to B$ and $\mathrm{d}^{*}B_{\varepsilon}\to\mathrm{d}^{*}B$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{T}^{2})$: since the exponent is purely imaginary the expectations converge by dominated convergence along a subsequence, while the semigroups converge weakly by strong resolvent convergence; see \cite[Sec.~15]{simon2005functional} for details.\relax{Note that in \cite[Thms~15.5 and~15.6]{simon2005functional}, the results are given on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ rather than the torus and the extension to rough $B$ there takes $B \in L^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but in Coulomb gauge. However, the arguments therein clearly extend to our present setting.}

Since $B$, and hence $\mathrm{d}^* B$, is $i \mathbb{R}$-valued, the exponent in \eqref{eq:FK} is purely imaginary, so the expectation in \eqref{eq:FK} has modulus at most one, which gives the first bound. Inserting it into the representation of Lemma~\ref{lem:semi-group} gives the second.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:neg_power_trace}
Let $B\in\Omega^1H^1$ and $\gamma>1$. For any $\lambda\geq 1$, the trace bound and its Hilbert--Schmidt consequence are
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\big( R_B(\lambda)^{\gamma}\big)\lesssim \lambda^{1-\gamma}, \qquad
\| R_B(\lambda)^{\gamma/2}\|_\mathrm{HS} \lesssim \sqrt{\lambda^{1-\gamma}}=\lambda^{\frac 1 2-\frac \gamma 2}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:Kato}
Let $B\in\Omega^1 L^2$ and $u\in W^{1,\infty}$.
Then for almost every $x$
\[
|\mathrm{d}|u| (x) |\leq |\mathrm{d}_Bu(x)|.
\]
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:Sobolev_comparison}
Let $p>2$ and $B\in \Omega^1 L^p$. Then for any $s\in [-1,1]$, we have $H^s=H^s_B$ and the following inequalities:
    \begin{align*}
    \|u\|_{H^s}&\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{L^p})^{|s|} \|u\|_{H^s_B}, \\
    \|u\|_{H^s_B}&\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{L^p})^{|s|} \|u\|_{H^s}.
    \end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By $C^\infty$ being a core of the covariant Laplacian, it is enough to consider $u\in C^\infty$. For $s=1$, we have
    \[
    \|u\|_{H^1_B}^2=\|\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{L^2}^2+\|u\|_{L^2}^2, \qquad
    \|\mathrm{d} |u|\|_{L^2}\leq \|\mathrm{d}_B u\|_{L^2}\leq \|u\|_{H^1_B}.
    \]
    For $r\geq 1$ with $\frac 1 r=\frac{1-\theta}{2}$ and $\theta\in[0,1]$, the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality gives
    \[
    \|u\|_{L^r}\lesssim \|\mathrm{d}|u|\|_{L^2}^\theta \|u\|_{L^2}^{1-\theta}.
    \]
    Since $1-\theta=\frac 2r$, for $r\geq 2$ this gives
    \[
     \|u\|_{L^r}\lesssim \|\mathrm{d}|u|\|_{L^2}^{1-\frac 2r} \|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac 2r}\lesssim \|u\|_{H^1_B}.
    \]
    Choose $r$ with $\frac 12=\frac 1p+\frac 1r$. The assumption $p>2$ excludes $r=\infty$. Then
    \begin{gather*}
    \|Bu\|_{L^2}\leq\|B\|_{L^p}\|u\|_{L^r}\lesssim \|B\|_{L^p}\|u\|_{H^1_B}, \\
    \|\mathrm{d} u\|_{L^2}=\|\mathrm{d}_B u+Bu\|_{L^2}\leq \|\mathrm{d}_B u\|_{L^2}+\|Bu\|_{L^2}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{L^p})\|u\|_{H^1_B}, \\
    \|u\|_{H^1}\leq (1+\|B\|_{L^p})\|u\|_{H^1_B}.
    \end{gather*}

    Conversely,
    \[
    \|\mathrm{d}_B u\|_{L^2}\leq \|\mathrm{d} u\|_{L^2}+\|Bu\|_{L^2}\lesssim \|u\|_{H^1}+\|B\|_{L^p}\|u\|_{L^r},
    \]
    and Sobolev embedding, $\|u\|_{L^r}\lesssim \|u\|_{H^1}$, gives
    \[
    \|u\|_{H^1_B}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{L^p})\|u\|_{H^1}.
    \]

    This proves the case $s=1$. For $s\in[0,1]$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:norm_comparison_pos_op} to $L_B+1$ and $L_0+1$ in either order. For $s\in[-1,0)$, use duality and boundedness of the identity map.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
In all of these bounds later on we take $B\in\Omega^1H^1$ and use Sobolev embedding to bound $\|B\|_{L^p}\lesssim \|B\|_{H^1}$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:derivative_regularity_reduction}
    For any $s\in [1,2]$, it holds that
    \[
    \|\mathrm{d}_B u\|_{H^{s-1}_B}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{s-1}\|u\|_{H^s_B}.
    \]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
We prove the endpoints and then interpolate. The case $s=1$ follows from
    $\|\mathrm{d}_B u\|_{L^2}\leq \|u\|_{H^1_B}$ by definition.

    For $s=2$, the identities $\mathrm{d}_B^*\mathrm{d}_B u=L_B$ and $\mathrm{d}_B \mathrm{d}_B u= \mathrm{d}_B^2 u=F^Bu$ give
\begin{align}\label{eq:energy_d_B_identity}
\|\mathrm{d}_B u\|_{\Omega^1 H^1_B}^2=\|\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{L^2}^2+\|L_Bu\|_{L^2}^2+\|F^Bu\|_{L^2}^2 .
\end{align}
We bound the three terms separately. The scalar Sobolev norm and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\begin{gather*}
\|L_Bu\|_{L^2}\leq \|(L_B+1)u\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{H_B^2}, \qquad
\|u\|_{L^2}\leq \|u\|_{H_B^2}, \\
\|\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{L^2}^2=\langle L_Bu,u\rangle
\leq \|L_Bu\|_{L^2}\|u\|_{L^2}
\leq \|u\|_{H_B^2}^2.
\end{gather*}
It remains to bound the curvature term. By Hölder,
\[
\|F^Bu\|_{L^2}\leq \|F^B\|_{L^2}\|u\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|B\|_{H^1}\|u\|_{L^\infty}.
\]
The diamagnetic inequality gives
\[
|u|
=
|(L_B+1)^{-1}(L_B+1)u|
\leq
(L_0+1)^{-1}|(L_B+1)u|,
\]
and since in two dimensions the kernel of $(L_0+1)^{-1}$ belongs to $L^2$, Young's inequality yields
\[
\|u\|_{L^\infty}
\lesssim
\|(L_B+1)u\|_{L^2}
=
\|u\|_{H_B^2}.
\]
Combining these estimates gives
\[
\|F^Bu\|_{L^2}
\lesssim
\|B\|_{H^1}\|u\|_{H_B^2}, \qquad
\|\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{\Omega^1 H_B^1}^2
\lesssim
\bigl(1+\|B\|_{H^1}^2\bigr)\|u\|_{H_B^2}^2,
\]
proving the case $s=2$.

The proof for the general case $s\in [1,2]$ follows by interpolation from Lemma~\ref{lem:interpolation_hilbert_scale}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:Sobolev_comparison_1forms}
Let $s\in [-1,1]$. One has $\Omega^1H^s=\Omega^1H^s_B$, and for any $\delta>0$, there exists $C_\delta>0$ such that
\begin{align*}
\|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^s}&\leq C_\delta (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{(1+\delta)|s|}\|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^s_B}, \\
\|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^s_B}&\leq C_\delta (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{(1+\delta)|s|}\|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^s}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
We again consider smooth $K\in\Omega^1C^\infty$ and argue the statement by approximation. By definition and the triangle inequality,
    \begin{align*}
    \|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^1_B}^2&=\|\mathrm{d}_B K\|_{L^2}^2+\|\mathrm{d}_B^* K\|_{L^2}^2+\|K\|_{L^2}^2, \\
    \|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^1} &\leq  \|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^1_B}+\|BK\|_{L^2}+\|B^*K\|_{L^2}.
    \end{align*}
    For $p,r$ with $\frac 1p+\frac 1r=\frac 1 2$,
    \[
    \|BK\|_{L^2}\leq \|B\|_{L^p}\|K\|_{L^r}.
    \]
    For $\theta\in[0,1]$ with $\frac{1}{r}=\frac{1-\theta}{2}$,
    \[
    \|K\|_{L^r}\lesssim \|\nabla |K|\|_{L^2}^\theta \|K\|_{L^2}^{1-\theta}.
    \]
    Kato's inequality  $|\nabla |K||\leq |\nabla_BK|$, with $\nabla_B$ denoting component-wise covariant derivatives, followed by direct computation gives
    \begin{gather*}
\|\nabla |K|\|_{L^2}^2\leq \|\nabla_BK\|_{L^2}^2\lesssim \|\mathrm{d}_B K\|_{L^2}^2+\|\mathrm{d}^*_BK\|_{L^2}^2+\int |\langle F^BK_1,K_2\rangle|.
    \end{gather*}
    Since
    \[
    \mathfrak{Re} \int \langle F^BK_1,K_2\rangle\lesssim \|F^B\|_{L^2}\|K\|_{L^4}^2, \qquad
    \|K\|_{L^4}^2\lesssim \|\nabla |K|\|_{L^2}\|K\|_{L^2},
    \]
    we obtain
    \[
    \|\nabla |K|\|_{L^2}^2\lesssim \|\mathrm{d}_B K\|_{L^2}^2+\|\mathrm{d}^*_BK\|_{L^2}^2+\|F^B\|_{L^2}\|\nabla |K|\|_{L^2}\|K\|_{L^2}.
    \]
    Young's inequality gives
    \[
    \|\nabla |K|\|_{L^2}^2\leq C(\|\mathrm{d}_B K\|_{L^2}^2+\|\mathrm{d}^*_BK\|_{L^2}^2+\|F^B\|_{L^2}^2\|K\|_{L^2}^2)+\frac 1 2\|\nabla |K|\|_{L^2}^2.
    \]
    Absorbing the last term on the right yields
    \begin{gather*}
    \|K\|_{L^r}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\theta}\|K\|_{\Omega^1H^1_B}^\theta \|K\|_{L^2}^{1-\theta}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\theta}\|K\|_{\Omega^1H^1_B}, \\
    \|K\|_{\Omega^1H^1}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+\theta}\|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^1_B}.
    \end{gather*}
    Since $\frac{1-\theta}2=\frac 1 2-\frac 1 p$, we have $1-\theta=1-\frac 2 p$ and $\theta=\frac 2 p$. Hence
  \[
    \|K\|_{\Omega^1H^1}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+\frac 2 p}\|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^1_B}.
    \]
    Taking $p$ arbitrarily large proves the claim.

    The reverse inequality is similar. As in Lemma~\ref{lem:Sobolev_comparison}, interpolation using Lemma~\ref{lem:norm_comparison_pos_op} and duality give both bounds for the remaining exponents.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:bounds_JAB}
Let $\kappa\in(0,1)$, let $s>1+\kappa$, and let
$\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ and $B\in\Omega^1H^1$.
Then, for every $\theta\in[0,1]$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|(J_{\mathbb{A},B}-J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})u\|_
{H_B^{-(1-\theta)\kappa-\theta s}}
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\kappa+2(s -1)}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
\|u\|_{H_B^{(1-\theta)s+\theta\kappa}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:J_operator_order}
Writing $d=1+3\kappa$, Lemma \ref{lem:bounds_JAB} with $s=1+2\kappa$ implies that $\|J_{\mathbb{A},B}-J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}\|_{H_B^p\to H_B^{p-d}}\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}$
for any $p\in[\kappa,1+2\kappa]$.
This shows we can treat $J_{\mathbb{A},B}-J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}$
as an operator of order $d$.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By interpolation (Lemma \ref{lem:interpolation_hilbert_scale}), it suffices to prove the estimate for $\theta=0$ and $\theta=1$.
Since each $J_{\mathbb{A},B},J_{
\bar\mathbb{A},B}$ is symmetric and $H^s_B$ is canonically dual to $H^{-s}_B$, the case $\theta=1$ follows immediately from the case $\theta=0$ by duality.
By monotonicity in $s$, it suffices to consider $s\in(1+\kappa,2]$.
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:Sobolev_comparison}
and the assumption $s>1+\kappa$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|(A-\bar A)^*\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{H_B^{-\kappa}}
&\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^\kappa
\|(A-\bar A)^*\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{H^{-\kappa}}
\\
&\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^\kappa
\|A-\bar A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}
\|\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{H^{s-1}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:Sobolev_comparison} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:derivative_regularity_reduction},
\[
\|\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{H^{s-1}}
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{s-1}
\|\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{H_B^{s-1}}
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2(s-1)}
\|u\|_{H_B^s}.
\]
Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bound_Ad_B}
\|(A-\bar A)^*\mathrm{d}_Bu\|_{H_B^{-\kappa}}
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\kappa+2(s-1)}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
\|u\|_{H_B^s}.
\end{equation}

For the zeroth-order term, choose $\delta\in(0,1)$ sufficiently small.
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|(A^2-\bar A^2)u\|_{H_B^{-\kappa}}
&\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^\kappa
\|(A^2-\bar A^2)u\|_{H^{-\kappa}}
\\
&\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^\kappa
\|A^2-\bar A^2\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}
\|u\|_{H^{(1+\delta)\kappa}}
\\
&\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{(2+\delta)\kappa}
\|A^2-\bar A^2\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}
\|u\|_{H_B^{(1+\delta)\kappa}}
\end{aligned}
\]
where we used Lemma~\ref{lem:Sobolev_comparison} in the last line.
Since $s>1+\kappa$, we may choose $\delta$ so that $(1+\delta)\kappa<s$ and $(2+\delta)\kappa\leq \kappa+2(s-1)$. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bound_dA_A2}
\|(A^2-\bar A^2)u\|_{H_B^{-\kappa}}
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\kappa+2(s-1)}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
\|u\|_{H_B^s}.
\end{equation}
Combining~\eqref{eq:bound_Ad_B} and~\eqref{eq:bound_dA_A2} gives
the claimed estimate for $\theta=0$ and $s\leq 2$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rem:map_block_A}
    Note that with the same way we proved~\eqref{eq:bound_Ad_B} using Lemma~\ref{lem:Sobolev_comparison_1forms}, we can prove
        \[
        \|A^*K\|_{ H^{-\kappa}_{\bar B}}\lesssim (1+\|\bar B\|_{H^1})^{4\kappa}\|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}\|K\|_{\Omega^1 H^{2\kappa}_B}, \qquad K\in\Omega^1 H^{2\kappa}_B.
        \]
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:resolvent_estimate}
Let $\kappa\in (0,\frac 14)$, $\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa} $ and $B\in\Omega^1H^1$.
Denote $d=1+3\kappa\in (1,7/4)$.
There exists a constant $C>0$ depending on $\kappa$, such that
\begin{align}\label{eq:resolvent_set_distinguished}
    \rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B}):=\Big\{z\in \mathbb{C}\colon \mathfrak{Re}(z)>0, \, \max\big\{1, C(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa} {\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}\big\}\leq  |z|^{1-\frac{d}{2}}\Big\},
\end{align}
satisfies $\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\subset \rho(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$. Moreover, for any $z\in\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$,
$s\in [-1-2\kappa,2-\kappa]$ and $\eta\in [0,2]\cap[s-1-2\kappa, s+2-\kappa]$, one has the resolvent estimate
\begin{equation}\label{eq:resolvent_estimate}
\|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)f\|_{H^{s}_B}\lesssim |z|^{\frac \eta2-1}\|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}.
\end{equation}
Finally, given another $\bar\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$, we have for any $z\in \rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\cap \rho_\star(L_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})$, the following continuity estimate:
\[
\|(R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(z))f\|_{H^{s}_B}\lesssim
|z|^{\frac \eta2-1}
|z|^{\frac{d}{2}-1}
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
\|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B},
\]
for any parameters $s$ and $\eta$ satisfying the conditions above.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Let $z\in\mathbb{C}$ satisfy $\mathfrak{Re}(z)>0$ and $|z|\geq 1$. The factorisation
    \[
    (L_{\mathbb{A},B}+z)=(L_B+z)+J_{\mathbb{A},B}=(L_B+z)(\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}),
    \]
    reduces invertibility to that of $\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}$, for which we use a Neumann series. For $p\in[\kappa,1+2\kappa]$ and $d=1+3\kappa$, Remark~\ref{rem:J_operator_order} gives
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:resolvent_JAB}
        \begin{aligned}
    \|R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}f\|_{H^{p}_B}&\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}\|R_B(z)\|_{H^{p-d}_B\to H^{p}_B} \|f\|_{H^{p}_B} \\
    &\leq C (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa} |z|^{\frac{d}{2} -1} \|f\|_{H^{p}_B}.
    \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    where the last bound uses Lemma~\ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical}.
    Since $\kappa<1/4$ implies $d<2$, we may choose $|z|$ large enough that
    \begin{align}\label{eq:choice_z}
    C (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa} |z|^{\frac{d}{2}-1}\leq \frac 1 2.
    \end{align}
    This is the condition defining $\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$ in~\eqref{eq:resolvent_set_distinguished}. The operator $(L_B+z)(\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})$ therefore has inverse
    \[
    T_z:=\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^k (R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k R_B(z).
    \]
    The map $T_z:L^2\to H^p_B\subset L^2$ is continuous. To identify its range, write
     \begin{align*}
     T_zf+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}T_zf&=\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^k (R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k R_B(z)f+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^k (R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k R_B(z)f\\
     &=\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^k (R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k R_B(z)f-\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^{k+1} (R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^{k+1} R_B(z)f\\
     &=R_B(z)f,
     \end{align*}
     and use the resolvent identity for $R_B(z)$ to obtain
     \begin{align*}
     T_z f+R_B(1)J_{\mathbb{A},B}T_z f&=T_z f+R_B(z) J_{\mathbb{A},B}T_z-(z-1) R_B(z) R_B(1) J_{\mathbb{A},B} T_z f\\
     &=R_B(z)f-(z-1) R_B(z) R_B(1)J_{\mathbb{A},B}T_z f.
     \end{align*}
    Taking $p=1+2\kappa$ gives $T_z f\in H^{1+2\kappa}_B$ and $T_z f+R_B(1)J_{\mathbb{A},B}T_z f\in H^2_B$, so $T_z f\in{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$.

     For injectivity, let $u\in{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$ satisfy $(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+z)u=0$. Invertibility of $L_B+z$ and $\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}$ gives
     \[
     (L_B+z)(\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})u=0
     \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})u=0
     \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=0.
     \]
     Thus $z\in\rho(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$, so $\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\subset\rho(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$ and $T_z=R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)$.

     For the resolvent estimate, take $z\in\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$ and write
     \begin{align}\label{eq:proof_resolvent_estimate_init_inequality}
     \|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)f\|_{H^s_B}=\|T_zf\|_{H^s_B}\leq \|R_B(z)f\|_{H^s_B}+ \sum_{k=1}^\infty \|(R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k R_B(z)f\|_{H^s_B}.
     \end{align}
     The first term is bounded by Lemma~\ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical}, since $\eta\in[0,2]$. For $k\geq1$, \eqref{eq:resolvent_JAB}-\eqref{eq:choice_z} give
     \begin{align*}
      \|(R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k &R_B(z)f\|_{H^s_B}\\
      &\leq \|R_B(z) J_{\mathbb{A},B}\|_{H^{p}_B \to H^s_B} \|(R_B(z) J_{\mathbb{A},B})^{k-1}\|_{H^{p}_B \to H^{p}_B}  \|R_B(z)f\|_{H^{p}_B} \\
      &\leq 2^{-(k-1)}\|R_B(z) J_{\mathbb{A},B}\|_{H^{p}_B \to H^s_B}   \|R_B(z)f\|_{H^{p}_B}.
     \end{align*}
    Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical}, provided $p-s+\eta \in [0,2]$,
    we obtain
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:s_eta_p}
     \|R_B(z)\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B\to H^{p}_B}\lesssim |z|^{\frac{p-s+\eta}{2}-1}
  \end{equation}
     Moreover, $\|J_{\mathbb{A},B}\|_{H^{p}_B \to H^{p-d}_B}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}$ by Remark~\ref{rem:J_operator_order}, thus,
provided $s-p+d\in [0,2]$, we have by Lemma ~\ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical} again,
     \begin{equation}\label{eq:p_s}
     \|R_B(z) J_{\mathbb{A},B}\|_{H^{p}_B \to H^s_B}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa} |z|^{\frac{s-p+d}{2}-1}.
     \end{equation}
     Therefore
    \begin{align*}
       \|(R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k R_B(z)f\|_{H^s_B}
       &\lesssim 2^{-(k-1)}
       |z|^{\frac{p-s+\eta}{2}-1}
       |z|^{\frac{s-p+d}{2}-1}
       (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa} \|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}
       \\
       &=
       2^{-(k-1)}
       |z|^{\frac{\eta}{2}-1}|z|^{\frac{d}{2}-1}
       (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa} \|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}.
     \end{align*}
    The conditions $s\in[-1-2\kappa,2-\kappa]$
    and $\eta\in[0,2]\cap[s-1-2\kappa, s+2-\kappa]$
    ensure that we can find $p\in [\kappa,1+2\kappa]$ such that $s-p+d\in [0,2]$ and
    $p-s+\eta\in [0,2]$.

    Using~\eqref{eq:choice_z} to estimate
    $|z|^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}\lesssim 1$
    leads to
     \[
      \|(R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^k R_B(z)f\|_{H^s_B}\lesssim 2^{-(k-1)} |z|^{\frac\eta 2-1}\|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}.
     \]
     Substituting into~\eqref{eq:proof_resolvent_estimate_init_inequality} yields
     \[
     \|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)f\|_{H^s_B}\lesssim |z|^{\frac\eta 2-1}\|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}.
     \]

     For continuity, take $z\in \rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\cap \rho_\star(L_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})$ and write
    \begin{align*}
      R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(z)&=((\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^{-1}-(\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})^{-1})R_B(z) \\
    &=-(\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})^{-1}(R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}-R_B(z)J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})(\operatorname{Id}+R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B})^{-1} R_B(z)\\
    &=-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(z) (J_{\mathbb{A},B}-J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z).
    \end{align*}
The resolvent estimate just proved gives
    \begin{align*}
    \|(R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(z))f\|_{H^s_B}
    &\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
    |z|^{\frac{s-p+d}{2}-1}
    |z|^{\frac{p-s+\eta}{2}-1}  \|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}\\
    &=
    |z|^{\frac\eta 2-1}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
    |z|^{\frac{d}{2}-1}  \|f\|_{H^{s-\eta}_B}.\qedhere
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:resolvent_identity}
Actually on the way, we have proved the resolvent identity
\[
R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)-R_B(z)=-R_B(z)J_{\mathbb{A},B}R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z).
\]
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:self_adjoint}
Let $\kappa\in (0,\frac 1 4)$,  $A\in \mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ and $B\in \Omega^1H^1$. Then the unbounded operator $(L_{\mathbb{A},B},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A},B}))$ is self-adjoint (and in particular densely defined and closed). Moreover, $B\in\Omega^1_\mathrm{C} H^1$, then  $(L_{\mathbb{A},B},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A},B}))=(L_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}))$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Both claims follow by approximating $\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ by smooth $\mathbb{A}_k\to\mathbb{A}$ in $\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa-\delta}$, with $\delta>0$ sufficiently small. For self-adjointness, note that
\[
\bigcap_{k\geq 0}\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A}_k,B})\cap \rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\cap\mathbb{R}\neq \varnothing
\]
by~\eqref{eq:resolvent_set_distinguished}. Fix such a $z$. Self-adjointness of $(L_{\mathbb{A}_k,B},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A}_k,B}))$ and operator-norm convergence $R_{\mathbb{A}_k,B}(z)\to R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)$ imply that $R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)$, and hence $(L_{\mathbb{A},B},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A},B}))$, is self-adjoint.

For $B\in\Omega^1_\mathrm{C} H^1$, the identity $(L_{\mathbb{A}_k,B},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A}_k,B}))=(L_{\mathbb{A}_k\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A}_k\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}))$ gives equal resolvents for each $k$. Their limits are $R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)$ and $R_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}(z)$, respectively, so $R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)=R_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}(z)$ and the limiting operators agree.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rem:spectral_theorem}
    The resolvent $R_{\mathbb{A},B}(z)$ is compact by $H^1\Subset L^2$ and $H^1_B\subset H^1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Sobolev_comparison}). Thus the spectrum of $(L_{\mathbb{A},B},{\mathscr{D}}(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$ consists of discrete real eigenvalues with finite-dimensional eigenspaces \cite[Prop.~2.11]{schmudgen2012}. The spectral theorem for self-adjoint unbounded operators gives an orthonormal eigenbasis $(e_i)_{i\geq0}$ and the representation
    \[
    L_{\mathbb{A},B}u=\sum_{i\geq 0} \lambda_i\langle u,e_i\rangle e_i,
    \]
     by \cite[Prop.~5.12]{schmudgen2012}, allowing us to use functional calculus.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{rem:fC_bound}
    Note that
\[
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)=(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)},
\]
with $\tau(\kappa)\to 0$ as $\kappa\to 0$, and the corresponding equality with $\bar\mathbb{A}=\0$ holds
\[
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)=(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}.
\]
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:difference_masses}
    Let $\kappa\in (0,\frac 1 4)$, $\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ and $B\in\Omega^1 H^1$.
    Denote $d=1+3\kappa$. Then
    \[
    |m_{\mathbb{A},B}-m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}|
    \lesssim
   {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)^{1/2}
    {\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
    \]
    Note that $m_{\0,B}=1$, since $L_{\0,B}=L_B\geq0$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
We set
\begin{align}\label{eq:m_star}
m_\star :=\min \rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\cap \mathbb{R}
=\max\big\{1, C(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\frac{10\kappa}{1-3\kappa}} {\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^{\frac{2}{1-3\kappa}}\big\}.
\end{align}
where we recall $\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$ from Theorem \ref{thm:resolvent_estimate}.
For another $\bar\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$,
we define $\bar m_\star$ similarly as $m_\star$, but with $\bar\mathbb{A}$. Set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:m_max_def}
m:=\max\{m_\star,\bar m_\star\},
\end{equation}
and note that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:m_bounded_by_fC}
m\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\frac{10\kappa}{1-3\kappa}}
(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{\frac{2}{1-3\kappa}}\lesssim {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)^{1/2}.
\end{equation}
Since $m\in \rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\cap \rho_\star(L_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})$, Theorem~\ref{thm:resolvent_estimate} gives $m+L_{\mathbb{A},B}>0$. The spectral relation and the min-max theorem for self-adjoint compact operators yield
\[
\max\sigma(R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m))
=\frac{1}{m+\min\sigma(L_{\mathbb{A},B})}
=
\sup_{\|f\|_{L^2}=1}
\langle R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m)f,f\rangle.
\]
Denote $J = J_{\mathbb{A},B} - J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}$.
Taking $p=\frac{d}{2}$ in Remark~\ref{rem:J_operator_order}, we obtain
\begin{align}\label{eq:J_symmetric_mass}
\|Ju\|_{H^{-d/2}_B}
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
\|u\|_{H^{d/2}_B}.
\end{align}

Using the resolvent identity,
\[
R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m)
=
-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m)
(J_{\mathbb{A},B}-J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})
R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m),
\]
self-adjointness of the resolvents, and~\eqref{eq:J_symmetric_mass}, we obtain for $\|f\|_{L^2}=1$
\begin{align*}
&\left|
\langle (R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m))f,f\rangle
\right|
\\
&\qquad\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
\|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m)f\|_{H^{d/2}_B}
\|R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m)f\|_{H^{d/2}_B}.
\end{align*}
Since $m\in\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})\cap\rho_\star(L_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})$, Theorem~\ref{thm:resolvent_estimate} (taking therein $s=\eta=d/2$) implies
\[
\|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m)f\|_{H^{d/2}_B}
+
\|R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m)f\|_{H^{d/2}_B}
\lesssim
m^{-1+\frac d4}\|f\|_{L^2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\left|
\max\sigma(R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m))
-
\max\sigma(R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m))
\right|
\lesssim
m^{-2+d/2}
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
\]

Set $f(x)=1+\max\{0,m-1/x\}$. By definition, $m_{\mathbb{A},B}=f(\max\sigma(R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m)))$. Since $f$ is $m^2$-Lipschitz, i.e. $|f(x)-f(y)|\leq m^2|x-y|$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
|m_{\mathbb{A},B}-m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}|
&\lesssim
m^{d/2}
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
\qedhere
\end{align*}
By~\eqref{eq:m_bounded_by_fC} together with the fact that $d=1+3\kappa\leq 2$, we get the desired estimate.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:resolvent_estimate_pushed}
Let $\kappa\in(0,\frac14)$, $\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ and
$B\in\Omega^1H^1$. Then, for every $\lambda\ge0$,
$s\in[-1-2\kappa,2-\kappa]$,
$\eta\in[0,2]\cap[s-1-2\kappa,s+2-\kappa]$,
one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pushed_resolvent}
\|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda+m_{\mathbb{A},B})\|_
{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{\frac\eta2-1}
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B).
\end{equation}
Moreover, denote $d=1+3\kappa$.
Then for $\bar\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$,
one has for every $\lambda\geq 0$ and $s,\eta$ as above
\begin{align}
\|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda+m_{\mathbb{A},B})
-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda+m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})\|_
{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{-2+\frac{\eta+d}{2}}
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)^2
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
\label{eq:pushed_resolvent_difference}
\end{align}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Recall $m_\star$ from~\eqref{eq:m_star} and note that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:m_star_local_bound}
m_\star
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\frac{10\kappa}{1-3\kappa}}
(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{\frac{2}{1-3\kappa}}
=
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)^{1/2}.
\end{equation}
Denote
\[
R_\lambda=R_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda+m_{\mathbb{A},B}),
\qquad
R_{\lambda,\star}=R_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda+m_\star).
\]
By \eqref{eq:resolvent_set_distinguished},
$\lambda+m_\star\in\rho_\star(L_{\mathbb{A},B})$, while the definition of $m_{\mathbb{A},B}$ in
\eqref{eq:m_def} implies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:m_def_bound}
\|R_\lambda\|_{L^2\to L^2}\le(1+\lambda)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, by Theorem \ref{thm:resolvent_estimate},
$1\leq m_{\mathbb{A},B}\le m_\star+1$
and thus
$|m_\star-m_{\mathbb{A},B}|\le m_\star$.

Recall the resolvent identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fist_resolv}
R_\lambda
=
R_{\lambda,\star}
+(m_\star-m_{\mathbb{A},B})R_{\lambda,\star}R_\lambda.
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:resolvent_estimate} with $(s,\eta)=(2-\kappa,0)$,
we have $\|R_{\lambda,\star}\|_{H_B^{2-\kappa}\to H_B^{2-\kappa}}\lesssim(\lambda+m_\star)^{-1}$.
On the other hand,
\eqref{eq:m_def_bound} and
\eqref{eq:resolvent_estimate} with
$(s,\eta)=(2-\kappa,2-\kappa)$ imply
\begin{align*}
\|(m_\star-m_{\mathbb{A},B})R_{\lambda,\star}R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{2-\kappa}\to H_B^{2-\kappa}}
&\leq
m_\star \|R_{\lambda,\star}\|_{L^2\to H^{2-\kappa}_B}
\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{2-\kappa}\to L^2}
\\
&\lesssim
m_\star(\lambda+m_\star)^{-\kappa/2}(1+\lambda)^{-1}
\leq
(1+\lambda)^{-1}m_\star^{(2-\kappa)/2}.
\end{align*}
Consequently $\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{2-\kappa}\to H_B^{2-\kappa}}\lesssim(1+\lambda)^{-1}m_\star^{(2-\kappa)/2}$.
By self-adjointness, duality and interpolation
(Lemma~\ref{lem:interpolation_hilbert_scale}),
for any $|q|\le2-\kappa$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pushed_same_space_sharp}
\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^q\to H_B^q}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{-1}m_\star^{|q|/2}.
\end{equation}
Now observe, by \eqref{eq:resolvent_estimate}, $\|R_{\lambda,\star}\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s} \lesssim (\lambda+m_\star)^{\frac{\eta}{2}-1}$,
and by \eqref{eq:pushed_same_space_sharp}
\[
\|R_{\lambda,\star}R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^{s}}
\leq
\|R_{\lambda,\star}\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\|R_{\lambda}\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^{s-\eta}}
\lesssim
(\lambda+m_\star)^{\frac{\eta}{2}-1}
(1+\lambda)^{-1}m_\star^{|s-\eta|/2}.
\]
Using again the resolvent identity \eqref{eq:fist_resolv} and $|m_\star-m_{\mathbb{A},B}|\le m_\star$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
&\lesssim
(\lambda+m_\star)^{\frac{\eta}{2}-1}
\{1+(1+\lambda)^{-1}m_\star^{1+|s-\eta|/2}\}
\\
&\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{\frac\eta2-1}
+
(1+\lambda)^{-1}
m_\star^{(\eta+|s-\eta|)/2}
\end{align*}
where we used $m_\star(\lambda+m_\star)^{\frac{\eta}{2}-1}\leq m_\star^{\eta/2}$.
The same estimate with $s'=\eta-s$ and $\eta'=\eta$ gives
\[
\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{-s}\to H_B^{\eta-s}}
=
\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s'-\eta'}\to H_B^{s'}}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{\frac\eta2-1}
+
(1+\lambda)^{-1}
m_\star^{(\eta+|s'-\eta|)/2}.
\]
The admissible range of $s,\eta$ is invariant under this duality transformation, so $\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}$ satisfies the same bound. Since $|s'-\eta|=|s|$, taking the better bound gives
\[
\|R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{\frac\eta2-1}
+
(1+\lambda)^{-1}
m_\star^{\frac{\eta}{2}+\alpha(s,\eta)},
\]
where
$
\alpha(s,\eta)
=
\min\{|s|,|s-\eta|\}/2.
$
Since $\frac{\eta}{2}+\alpha(s,\eta)\leq3/2$ by considering the signs of $s$ and $s-\eta$, together with~\eqref{eq:m_star_local_bound} this then  proves~\eqref{eq:pushed_resolvent}.

For the difference estimate, recall $m$ defined in~\eqref{eq:m_max_def}.
Write $\bar R_\lambda = R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda+m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})$.
By the resolvent identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:resolv_diff}
R_\lambda-\bar R_\lambda
=
-\bar R_\lambda
\bigl(
J_{\mathbb{A},B}-J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}
+m_{\mathbb{A},B}-m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}
\bigr)
R_\lambda.
\end{equation}
By the analogous estimates to
\eqref{eq:s_eta_p}-\eqref{eq:p_s}
with Lemma \ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical}
replaced by the intermediate bound
\[
\|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda+m_{\mathbb{A},B})\|_
{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{\frac\eta2-1}m_\star^{3/2},
\]
and the corresponding bound for $\bar\mathbb{A}$, we obtain
\begin{align}\label{eq:proof_pushed_resolvent}
\|\bar R_\lambda
(J_{\mathbb{A},B}-J_{\bar\mathbb{A},B})
R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{-2+\frac{\eta+d}{2}}
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}
m^3
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
\end{align}
Using~\eqref{eq:m_bounded_by_fC}, we have
$
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{5\kappa}m^3
\lesssim
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)^2,
$
and hence the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:proof_pushed_resolvent} is bounded by the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:pushed_resolvent_difference}.

Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:difference_masses}, combined with the intermediate pushed resolvent estimate above with
\eqref{eq:pushed_same_space_sharp} shows
\[
\|\bar R_\lambda R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{-2+\eta/2}
m^{\frac{\eta}{2}+\alpha(s,\eta)}m^{\alpha(s,\eta)}.
\]
Note that $\frac{\eta}{2}+2\alpha(s,\eta)\leq 2$, and therefore, by~\eqref{eq:m_bounded_by_fC},
\[
\|\bar R_\lambda R_\lambda\|_{H_B^{s-\eta}\to H_B^s}
\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{-2+\eta/2}
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B).
\]
Thus the term with the mass difference in \eqref{eq:resolv_diff} is bounded by
\[
(1+\lambda)^{-2+\eta/2}
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)^{3/2}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa},
\]
which is also bounded by a multiple of the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:pushed_resolvent_difference}.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:fractional_power_comparison_LAB}
Let $\kappa\in (0,\frac 14)$, $\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa} $ and $B\in\Omega^1H^1$.
Then for all $\theta\in[0,1]$ and  $u\in{\mathscr{D}}((L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^\theta)$, one has
\[
\|u\|_{H_B^{\theta(2-\kappa)}}\lesssim {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)^\theta \|(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^\theta u\|_{L^2}.
\]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The resolvent estimate at $s=2-\kappa$ gives the first bound for every $f\in L^2$, and taking $f=(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})u$ afterwards, gives the second:
\begin{gather*}
\|R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\mathbb{A},B})f\|_{H_B^{2-\kappa}}\lesssim {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)\|f\|_{L^2}, \\
\|u\|_{H_B^{2-\kappa}}\lesssim {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B) \|(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})u\|_{L^2}.
\end{gather*}
Interpolation by Lemma~\ref{lem:norm_comparison_pos_op} with the positive self-adjoint operators $(L_B+1)$ and $(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})$ gives, for every $\theta\in[0,1]$,
\[
\|u\|_{H_B^{\theta(2-\kappa)}}=\|(L_B+1)^{\theta(2-\kappa)/2}u\|_{L^2}
\lesssim {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)^\theta\|(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^\theta u\|_{L^2}.
\]
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
Note that $i\in\{-1,0,2\}$ in $\Xi_i$ can be viewed as the amount the operator $X\in\Xi_i$ regularises.  For example, a derivative regularises by $-1$ and a resolvent by $2$.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
\label{rem:fC_bound_power_counting}
    By Remark~\ref{rem:fC_bound}, we have that $\boldsymbol{\big[}R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda)\boldsymbol{\big]}$ are bounded by $(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}$ and similar statement for the difference of resolvents.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:maps_0_order}
    For any $f\in C^{-\kappa/2}$ or $K\in\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}$, we have
    \[
   \|f\|_{\Omega^0 H^{2\kappa}_B\to \Omega^0 H^{-\kappa}_B }\lesssim \boldsymbol{\big[}f\boldsymbol{\big]}, \qquad \|K^*\|_{\Omega^1 H^{2\kappa}_B\to \Omega^0 H^{-\kappa}_B} \lesssim \boldsymbol{\big[}K\boldsymbol{\big]}.
    \]
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
One should just note that the this is Young multiplication theorem where we move between the Sobolev spaces $H^s$ and $H^s_B$ (or $\Omega^1H^s$ and $\Omega^1H^s_B$) which yields the corresponding powers in $(1+\|B\|_{H^1})$ (note that for the $1$-form Sobolev comparison Lemma~\ref{lem:Sobolev_comparison_1forms} we lose an additional $\kappa$).
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:power_counting}
Let $k\geq2$ be an integer and $(X_j)_{j=1}^k\subset\Xi$ have well-defined composition $\prod_{j=1}^k X_j$. Assume
\[
X_1,X_k\in\Xi_2,\qquad
X_j=\mathrm{d}_B\implies X_{j+1}\in\Xi_2,\qquad
X_j\in\Xi_0\implies X_{j-1},X_{j+1}\not\in\Xi_0.
\]
Then $\prod_{j=1}^k X_j$ is trace class and
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\Big|\prod_{j=1}^k X_j\Big|\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa}\prod_{j=1}^k \boldsymbol{\big[}X_j\boldsymbol{\big]}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
If cyclicity were true, then
    \begin{align*}
\operatorname{Tr}\Big(\prod_{j=1}^k X_j\Big)
&=\operatorname{Tr}\Big((L_B+1)^{-1-\kappa/2} (L_B+1)^{1-\kappa/2}  \Big(\prod_{j=1}^k X_j\Big) (L_B+1)^{\kappa} \Big),
\end{align*}
which means that the composition of operators is trace class if
\[
\Big\|\prod_{j=1}^k X_j\Big\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{2-\kappa}_B}<\infty,
\]
in which case we get
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{Tr}\Big|\prod_{j=1}^k X_j\Big|&\leq \operatorname{Tr}((L_B+1)^{-1-\kappa/2}) \Big\|\prod_{j=1}^k X_j\Big\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{2-\kappa}_B}.
\end{align*}
A resolvent $R\in\Xi_2$ allows any neighbouring operators. By the hypotheses, each derivative is followed by a resolvent and, to return from $1$-forms to $0$-forms, preceded by $K^*$ with $K\in\Omega^1C^{-\kappa/2}$. Thus derivatives and $1$-forms occur in blocks $K^*\mathrm{d}_B R$, while $f\in C^{-\kappa/2}$ occurs as $fR$. The available blocks are
\[
R, \qquad fR, \qquad K^*\mathrm{d}_B R , \qquad f,K\in\Xi_0, R\in\Xi_2.
\]
Write $\prod_{j=1}^k X_j=\prod_{j=1}^\ell Y_j$, where the $Y_j$ are these blocks and $Y_1=X_1\in\Xi_2$.

For $R\in\Xi_2$, $f\in C^{-\kappa/2}$ and $K\in\Omega^1C^{-\kappa/2}$, the first two bounds follow from Lemma~\ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical}, Theorem~\ref{thm:resolvent_estimate_pushed} and Young's multiplication theorem. For the third, we also use Proposition~\ref{prop:derivative_regularity_reduction}:
\begin{gather*}
\|R\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{-\kappa}_B}\leq \|R\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{2\kappa}_B}\lesssim \boldsymbol{\big[}R\boldsymbol{\big]},  \qquad \|fR\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{-\kappa}_B}\lesssim \boldsymbol{\big[}f\boldsymbol{\big]} \boldsymbol{\big[}R\boldsymbol{\big]}, \\
\|K^*\mathrm{d}_BR\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{-\kappa}_B}\lesssim \boldsymbol{\big[}K\boldsymbol{\big]}\boldsymbol{\big[}\mathrm{d}_B\boldsymbol{\big]}\boldsymbol{\big[}R\boldsymbol{\big]}.
\end{gather*}
In particular
\[
\Big\| \prod_{j=1}^\ell Y_j \Big\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{2-\kappa}_B}\lesssim \|X_1\|_{H^{-\kappa}_B\to H^{2-\kappa}_B}\prod_{j=2}^\ell \|Y_j\|_{H^{-2\kappa}_B\to H^{-\kappa}_B}\lesssim \|X_1\|_{H^{-\kappa}_B\to H^{2-\kappa}_B}\prod_{j=2}^k \boldsymbol{\big[}X_j\boldsymbol{\big]},
\]
by the block decomposition. Lemma~\ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical} and Theorem~\ref{thm:resolvent_estimate_pushed} give
\[
\|X_1\|_{H^{-\kappa}_B\to H^{2-\kappa}_B}\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa}\boldsymbol{\big[}X_1\boldsymbol{\big]},
\]
which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:Pi_quadratic_form}
  For $\kappa\in [0,1/4)$ the following bound and its $L^1$ consequence hold:
  \[
| \boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda(A,B)| \lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 3 2 +\kappa}\|B\|_{H^1} \|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}, \qquad
\| \boldsymbol{\Pi}(A,B)\|_{L^1}\lesssim  \|B\|_{H^1} \|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}.
  \]
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:vac_pol_bound}
    The operator $\Pi^\lambda$ is transverse, meaning that
    \[
    \sum_{k=1}^2 \Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(p)p_k = 0 \quad\textup{ for all }\, j\in\{1,2\},
    \]
    and satisfies the spectral bound
    \[
    |\Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(p)| \lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-2} + \begin{cases}
        |p|^2(1+\lambda)^{-2} &\textup{ if }\quad |p|\le \sqrt{1+\lambda} \\
        (1+\lambda)^{-1} &\textup{ if }\quad |p|> \sqrt{1+\lambda}
    \end{cases}
    \]
    for all $j,k=1,2$ and $p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
We first verify transversality. With the help of the identity
   \[
   (2q+p)\cdot p = (1+\lambda+|p+q|^2)-(1+\lambda+|q|^2),
   \]
   we find that
   \[
   \sum_{k=1}^2 \Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(p)p_k = \sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2} \frac{p_j}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^2}-\frac{(2q+p)_j}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^2}+\frac{(2q+p)_j}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)(1+\lambda+|p+q|^2)}.
   \]
   The first summand cancels part of the second; the remaining sums vanish by antisymmetry under $q\mapsto -q$ and $q\mapsto -q-p$, respectively. For $p\ne0$, $\Pi^\lambda(p)$ acts as a scalar multiple of the rank one projection onto the transverse component. It therefore has the form
   \begin{align*}
   \Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(p) &= \operatorname{Tr}\Pi^\lambda(p) \Big(\delta_{j,k}-\frac{p_j p_k}{|p|^2}\Big) \,\textup{ for }\, p\neq 0,\\
   \Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(0) &= \delta_{j,k}\sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2}\frac{1+\lambda-|q|^2}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^3},
   \end{align*}
   where the trace is over the internal indices.
   We estimate the zero mode first, since we will use this bound again below. The sum converges absolutely for each $\lambda$. We show that cancellation between the terms on either side of $|q|^2=1+\lambda$ gives an integrable bound in $\lambda$. To see this, define $h_\lambda$ and observe that
   \[
   h_\lambda(x) = \frac{1+\lambda-|x|^2}{(1+\lambda+|x|^2)^3}, \qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\; h_\lambda(x)\,\mathrm{d} x = 0.
   \]
   Since $h_\lambda$ is smooth and decays as $O(|x|^{-4})$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$, Poisson summation gives the identity
   \[
   \sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2}\frac{1+\lambda-|q|^2}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^3} = \frac{1}{4\pi^2}\sum_{\substack{\xi\in{\mathbb Z}^2 \\ \xi\neq 0}} \hat h_\lambda(\xi) = \frac{1}{4\pi^2(1+\lambda)}\sum_{\substack{\xi\in{\mathbb Z}^2 \\ \xi\neq 0}} \hat h_0\big(\sqrt{1+\lambda}\,\xi\big),
   \]
   where the last equality follows by rescaling the Fourier transform. Since $\hat h_0(\xi)$ decays as $O\big((1+|\xi|)^{-n}\big)$ for every $n$, we obtain $|\Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(0)| \lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-2}$.
   We address $\operatorname{Tr}\Pi^\lambda(p)$ for $|p|^2>1+\lambda$ next. Split the lattice sum according to $D_1 \coloneqq \{|q|\le |p|/2\}$, $D_2 \coloneqq \{|q+p|\le |p|/2\}$ and $D_3 \coloneqq 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2\setminus(D_1\cup D_2)$. On $D_1$, it holds that $1+\lambda + |p+q|^2 \ge |p|^2/2$, which implies the inequality
   \begin{align*}
   \sum_{q\in D_1} \frac{2(1+\lambda -|q|^2) + |p|^2}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^2(1+\lambda+|q+p|^2)} &\lesssim \sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2} \frac{1}{(1+\lambda +|q|^2)^2} + \frac{1}{|p|^2}\sum_{q\in D_1} \frac{1}{1+\lambda +|q|^2} \\
   &\lesssim \frac{1}{1+\lambda} + \frac{1}{1+\lambda}\frac{\log\big(1+\frac{|p|^2}{1+\lambda}\big)}{\frac{|p|^2}{1+\lambda}} \lesssim \frac{1}{1+\lambda}.
   \end{align*}
   The estimate for $D_2$ runs along similar lines after the change of lattice variables $q\mapsto p+q$, and for the complement piece $D_3$ we have the bound
   \begin{multline*}
   \sum_{q\in D_3} \frac{2(1+\lambda -|q|^2) + |p|^2}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^2(1+\lambda+|q+p|^2)} \lesssim \sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2\setminus D_1} \frac{1}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^2} \\
   + \sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2\setminus D_2} \frac{1}{(1+\lambda+|p+q|^2)^2} \lesssim \sum_{|r|\ge |p|/2} \frac{1}{(1+\lambda+|r|^2)^2} \lesssim \frac{1}{1+\lambda + |p|^2} \sim \frac{1}{1+\lambda}.
   \end{multline*}
   For $|p|^2\le 1+\lambda$, the zero-mode estimate reduces the proof to bounding $\operatorname{Tr}\big(\Pi^\lambda(p)-\Pi^\lambda(0)\big)$. With $a\coloneqq 1+\lambda+|q|^2$, $b\coloneqq 1+\lambda+|p+q|^2$ and $c\coloneqq 1+\lambda-|q|^2$, we have
   \begin{align*}
   \operatorname{Tr}\big(\Pi^\lambda(p)-\Pi^\lambda(0)\big) &= \sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2} \frac{2(1+\lambda -|q|^2) + |p|^2}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^2(1+\lambda+|q+p|^2)} -  \frac{2(1+\lambda -|q|^2)}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^3} \\
   &= \sum_{q\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2} \frac{2(2p\cdot q+|p|^2)^2}{a^4b} + \frac{|p|^2}{a^2b} - \frac{2c(2p\cdot q+|p|^2)}{a^4}.
   \end{align*}
   Part of the third term above is odd in $q$ and thus vanishes, and the remaining terms can immediately be simplified by the inequality $|c|\le a$. Using $|p|^2 \le 1+\lambda$, the estimates
   \[
   \frac{2(2p\cdot q+|p|^2)^2}{a^3 b} + \frac{|p|^2}{a^2b} + \frac{2|p|^2}{a^3} \le \frac{16|p|^2|q|^2 + 4|p|^4}{a^3b} + \frac{3|p|^2}{(1+\lambda) a^2} \lesssim \frac{|p|^2}{(1+\lambda) a^2}
   \]
   are straightforward and yield the desired $|p|^2/(1+\lambda)^2$ bound after summing in $q$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:vac_pol_bound} and repeated applications of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality yields
    \begin{align*}
        |\boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda (A,B)| &\le \sum_{j,k=1}^2 \Big[ \Big((1+\lambda)^{-2}\Big(\sum_{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2} + \sum_{|p|^2\le 1+\lambda} |p|^2\Big) + (1+\lambda)^{-1}\sum_{|p|^2>1+\lambda} \Big] |\hat A_j(p)||\hat B_k(p)| \\
        &\le \sum_{j,k=1}^2(1+\lambda)^{-2}\Big(\sum_{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2}\langle p\rangle^{-4\kappa} |\hat A_j(p)|^2\sum_{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2}\langle p\rangle^{4\kappa} |\hat B_k(p)|^2\Big)^{1/2} \\
        &\quad\quad\quad\quad + (1+\lambda)^{-2}\Big(\sum_{|p|^2\le 1+\lambda}\langle p\rangle^{-2+6\kappa} \sum_{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2}\langle p\rangle^{2-6\kappa} |\hat A_j(p)|^2|\hat B_k(p)|^2\Big)^{1/2} \\
        &\quad\quad\quad\quad + (1+\lambda)^{-3/2+\kappa} \sum_{|p|^2> 1+\lambda}\langle p\rangle^{1-2\kappa} |\hat A_j(p)||\hat B_k(p)|.
        \end{align*}
        By standard embeddings on $\mathbb{T}^2$, we thus obtain the bound
        \begin{align*}
        |\boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda (A,B)| &\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-2}\|A\|_{\Omega^1 H^{-2\kappa}} \|B\|_{\Omega^1 H^{2\kappa}} + (1+\lambda)^{-2+3\kappa}\|A\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}} \|B\|_{\Omega^1 H^{1-\kappa}} \\
        &\quad\quad\quad\quad + (1+\lambda)^{-3/2+\kappa}\|A\|_{\Omega^1 H^{-2\kappa}} \|B\|_{\Omega^1 H^1} \\
        &\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-3/2+\kappa}\|A\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}} \|B\|_{\Omega^1 H^1},
     \end{align*}
     for all $\kappa<1/4$, which establishes the claim.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:translation_determinant}
   Let $\kappa\in(0,\frac 14)$, $\mathbf{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}_{\mathrm{V}}$ and $B\in\Omega^1_\mathrm{C} H^1$. It holds that
    \[
    \mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0)=\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},B).
    \]
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
By definition,
\begin{align*}
\begin{split}
\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0)&:=-(m_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}-1)\int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}( R_0(\lambda+1)^2)\,\mathrm{d} \lambda \\
&\qquad +   \int_0^N \big( \mathbb{V}(\lambda)+\boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda(2A+B,B)-\operatorname{Tr}{\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}(\lambda) \big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda  \\
&\qquad+  \int_0^N  \operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
\end{split}
\end{align*}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:self_adjoint}, $m_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}=m_{\mathbb{A},B}$. Also,
\[
{\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}(\lambda)={\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)+R_0(\lambda+1)-R_B(\lambda+1).
\]
Writing the trace in Fourier variables gives
\[
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda(2A+B,B)-\operatorname{Tr}{\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A}\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,0}(\lambda)=-\operatorname{Tr}{\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda).
\]
Substituting these identities into~\eqref{eq:def_cQ_N} proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:convergence_cQ_N}
    Let $\kappa\in (0,\frac 1{12})$ and $\mathbf{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}_{\mathrm{V}}$. The limit of $\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},0)$ as $N\to\infty$ exists and is denoted by $\mathcal{Q}_\infty(\mathbb{A},0)$. Furthermore, one has the identity
    \[
\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},0)= \int_0^N \mathbb{V}(\lambda)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda +  \int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}({\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda, \qquad N\in [0,\infty].
    \]
   Finally, for any $N\in [0,\infty]$, one has
   \[
   |\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},0)-\mathcal{Q}_N(\bar\mathbf{A},0)|\lesssim (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)} {\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}-\bar\mathbf{A}\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa}.
   \]
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
By the definition of $\mathcal{Q}_N$ in~\eqref{eq:def_cQ_N} and the decomposition of ${\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},0}$ from~\eqref{eq:def_cQ_N}, we get
    \begin{align*}
\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},0)&:=-(m_{\mathbb{A},0}-1)\int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}( R_0(\lambda+1)^2)\,\mathrm{d} \lambda +   \int_0^N \big( \mathbb{V}(\lambda)-\operatorname{Tr}{\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda) \big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda  \\
&\qquad + \sum_{i=1}^3\int_0^N  \operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},0}^i(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda+ \int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}({\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda,
\end{align*}
where we have used that each term in the decomposition of ${\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},0}$ is trace class on its own and integrable when $N<\infty$. We know that ${\mathscr q}^2$ cancels with the corresponding term next to $\mathbb{V}$ and the ${\mathscr q}^3$ term cancels with the mass term in the beginning of the expression. Finally,
\begin{align}\label{eq:tr_q1_vanishes}
\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^1_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda))=2\operatorname{Tr}(A^*\mathrm{d} R_0(1+\lambda)^2)=0,
\end{align}
 due to the fact that $R_0(1+\lambda)^2$  is translation invariant and even, so its derivative vanishes on the diagonal.   Hence for $N<\infty$
\[
\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},0)= \int_0^N \mathbb{V}(\lambda)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda +  \int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}({\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
\]
Now Lemma~\ref{lem:Rem_det} below (with $B=0$) implies the integrability required for the remainder term to take $N\to\infty$ and the continuity estimate.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:Rem_det}
Let $\kappa\in(0,\frac 14)$, $\mathbb{A}\in \mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ and $B\in \Omega^1 H^1$ in the Coulomb gauge. Then we have
\begin{align}\label{eq:rem_bound}
|\operatorname{Tr} ({\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))| \lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 32+6\kappa } (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}.
\end{align}
Moreover, given another $\bar\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$, we have
\[
|\operatorname{Tr} ({\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)-{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))| \lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 32+6\kappa }(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)} {\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Write $R_B:=R_B(1+\lambda)$ and $R_{\mathbb{A},B}:=R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda)$. Define
\begin{gather*}
C_{\mathbb{A}}:=1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}, \qquad C_B:=1+\|B\|_{H^1}, \qquad \mu:=1+\lambda,\\
J^{m;0}_{\mathbb{A},B}:=(A^2+m_{\mathbb{A},B}-1).
\end{gather*}
Here $J^{m;0}_{\mathbb{A},B}$ is the zero order part of $J^m_{\mathbb{A},B}$.
We write  ${\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}:={\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)$ and we split it as follows:
\[
{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)=8{\mathrm{Rem}}^1+4{\mathrm{Rem}}^2-2{\mathrm{Rem}}^3-2{\mathrm{Rem}}^4-{\mathrm{Rem}}^5,
\]
where
\begin{alignat*}{2}
{\mathrm{Rem}}^1&:= R_BA^*\mathrm{d}_B R_B A^*\mathrm{d}_B R_B A^*\mathrm{d}_B R_{\mathbb{A},B},
&\qquad {\mathrm{Rem}}^2&:= R_BA^*\mathrm{d}_B R_B A^*\mathrm{d}_B R_B J^{m;0}_{\mathbb{A},B}R_{\mathbb{A},B},\\
{\mathrm{Rem}}^3&:=R_BJ_{\mathbb{A},B}^{m;0}R_B A^*\mathrm{d}_B R_{\mathbb{A},B},
&\qquad {\mathrm{Rem}}^4&:=R_B A^*\mathrm{d}_B R_B J_{\mathbb{A},B}^{m;0} R_{\mathbb{A},B},\\
{\mathrm{Rem}}^5&:=R_B J^{m;0}_{\mathbb{A},B} R_B J_{\mathbb{A},B}^{m;0} R_{\mathbb{A},B}.
\end{alignat*}

Using the power counting setting from Section~\ref{sec:power_counting}, we apply Lemma~\ref{lem:power_counting} to bound the traces of ${\mathrm{Rem}}^i$. Its assumptions are easily verified. Define $\tilde\Xi_0:=\{J^{m;0}_{\mathbb{A},B}\}\cup\{A\}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:difference_masses} gives
\begin{align}\label{eq:regularity_J_0_order}
\|J^{m;0}_{\mathbb{A},B}\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}.
\end{align}
To treat ${\mathrm{Rem}}^1$, we note that we have four resolvents and three derivatives, and as such we get by  Lemmas~\ref{lem:maps_0_order} and~\ref{lem:power_counting}
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{Tr}|{\mathrm{Rem}}^1|&\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa}(1+\lambda)^{4\cdot(-1+2\kappa)} (1+\lambda)^{3\cdot\frac 1 2} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}\\
&\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 3 2+6\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}.
\end{align*}
Regarding ${\mathrm{Rem}}^2$, we count four resolvents and two derivatives and such we get together with~\eqref{eq:regularity_J_0_order}
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{Tr}|{\mathrm{Rem}}^2|&\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa}(1+\lambda)^{4\cdot(-1+2\kappa)} (1+\lambda)^{2\cdot\frac 1 2} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}\\
&\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-2+6\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}.
\end{align*}
For the remaining terms, the same power counting argument gives
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{Tr}|{\mathrm{Rem}}^3|&\lesssim   (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 32+4\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}\\
\operatorname{Tr}|{\mathrm{Rem}}^4|&\lesssim   (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 3 2+4\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}\\
\operatorname{Tr}|{\mathrm{Rem}}^5|&\lesssim   (1+\lambda)^{-2+4\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}.
\end{align*}
Combining these bounds yields~\eqref{eq:rem_bound}.

For the continuity estimate, we repeat the bounds, inserting the differences $A-\bar A$, $J^{m;0}_{\mathbb{A},B}-J^{m;0}_{\bar \mathbb{A},B}$ and $R_{\mathbb{A},B}-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}$ in each term. The same bounds then hold with the additional factor ${\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:lower_bound_det}
    Let $\kappa\in (0,\frac 1{12})$, $\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}_{\mathrm{V}}$ and $B\in\Omega^1 H^1$ in the Coulomb gauge. We have the following lower bound uniformly in $N\in [0,N]$:
    \[
\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},B) \geq -C(1+{\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}-\delta \|B\|_{H^1}^{1+\tau(\kappa)}.
    \]
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:differentiating_resolvents}
For any $\lambda>0$, the map $\theta\mapsto R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)$ is twice differentiable as a map $(0,1)\to {\mathrm{L}}(H^{-\kappa},H^{2-\kappa})$ for any $\kappa\in [0,\frac14)$, and we have
\begin{align*}
\partial_\theta R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)&=-2R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)B^*\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)\\
\partial_\theta^2 R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)&=8R_{B_\theta}(\lambda) B^* \mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)B^*\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)-2R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)B^*BR_{B_\theta}(\lambda).
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
It is clear that $R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)$ maps $L^2$ to $H^2$. Let $\theta\in (0,1)$ and $h\in\mathbb{R}$ be close enough to zero, and write
\[
L_{B_{\theta+h}}-L_{B_\theta}=2h B^*\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}+h^2B^*B.
\]
Note that uniformly in $\theta\in [0,1]$
\begin{gather*}
\|B^*\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}u\|_{L^2}\lesssim \|B\|_{L^4}\|\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}u\|_{L^4}\lesssim \|B\|_{H^1}(\|Bu\|_{L^4}+\| u\|_{W^{1,4}})\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^2 \|u\|_{H^{2-\kappa}},\\
\|B^*B u\|_{L^2}\leq \|B\|_{L^4}^2\|u\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \|B\|_{H^1}^2\|u\|_{H^{2-\kappa}},\\
\text{so that}\qquad \|L_{B_{\theta+h}}-L_{B_\theta}\|_{H^2\to L^2}\lesssim |h| (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^2.
\end{gather*}
Now we apply the resolvent identity
    \begin{align*}
    R_{B_{\theta+h}}(\lambda)-R_{B_\theta}(\lambda) &=-R_{B_{\theta+h}}(\lambda) (L_{B_{\theta+h}}-L_{B_\theta})R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)\\ &= -R_{B_{\theta+h}}(\lambda) (2h B^*\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}+h^2B^*B)R_{B_\theta}(\lambda),
        \end{align*}

    from where we see continuity of $\theta\mapsto R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)$ and that
    \[
    \lim_{h\to 0}\Big\|\frac{R_{B_{\theta+h}}(\lambda)-R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)}{h}+2R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)B^*\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}R_{B_\theta}(\lambda)\Big\|_{L^2\to H^2}=0,
    \]

    yielding differentiability and the identity of the first derivative.

    The second derivative follows from the product rule and differentiability of $\theta\mapsto \mathrm{d}_{B_\theta}$ as a map $H^2\to H^1$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:differentiation_trace}
Assume an operator $[0,1]\ni\theta\mapsto X_\theta$ is differentiable as a map $(0,1)\to {\mathrm{L}}(L^2)$ with derivative $\dot X_\theta$. If $X_\theta$ and $\dot X_\theta$ are both trace class with trace class norms bounded uniformly in $\theta$, then
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(X_\theta)-\operatorname{Tr}(X_0)=\int_0^\theta \operatorname{Tr}(\dot X_\rho)\,\mathrm{d}\rho\]
Furthermore, if $X_\theta$ is twice differentiable with trace class derivatives, we get
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(X_\theta)-\operatorname{Tr}(X_0)-\operatorname{Tr}(\dot X_0)=\int_0^\theta \int_0^\rho \operatorname{Tr}(\ddot X_\eta) \,\mathrm{d} \eta\,\mathrm{d} \rho=\int_0^\theta (\theta-\rho) \operatorname{Tr}(\ddot X_\rho)\,\mathrm{d} \rho.
\]
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
We start by writing
    \begin{align*}
   {\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},B}&={\mathscr q}_{A,B}^1+{\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},B}^2 +{\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},B}^3+{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}\\
   &={\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},0}+\tilde{\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}+{\mathscr q}^1_{A,B}+ ({\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},B}-{\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},0})+({\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}-\tilde{\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B})+{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B},
    \end{align*}
    where $\tilde{\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},B}^3(\lambda)=(m_{\mathbb{A},B}-1)R_0(1+\lambda)^2$. We obtain after cancelling the terms ${\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},B}^2$ and $\tilde{\mathscr q}_{\mathbb{A},B}^3$ (the mass term) that
   \begin{align}\label{eq:Q_N_rewritten}
   \begin{split}
\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A},B)
&=  \int_0^N  \mathbb{V}(\lambda)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
 +  \int_0^N  \operatorname{Tr}{\mathscr q}^1_{A,B}(\lambda) \,\mathrm{d}\lambda \\
&\qquad + \int_0^N
\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)-{\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda \\
&\qquad + \int_0^N
\operatorname{Tr} ({\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)-\tilde{\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
+ \int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}({\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\\
&\qquad + \int_0^N
\operatorname{Tr}(R_0(1+\lambda)-R_B(1+\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
\end{split}
\end{align}
The first integral is bounded by $\|\mathbb{V}\|_{L^1}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:Rem_det}, the remainder is integrable in $\lambda$ and satisfies
\[
\Big| \int_0^N \operatorname{Tr} ({\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\Big|\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)} (1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}.
\]
Finally, by diamagnetic inequality,
\[
\int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}(R_0(1+\lambda)-R_B(1+\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\geq 0.
\]
It remains to estimate the three terms involving ${\mathscr q}^i_{\mathbb{A},B}$ using power counting Lemma~\ref{lem:power_counting}.

\@startsection{paragraph}{4}{\z@}{1.5ex \@plus .5ex \@minus .2ex}{-1em}{\normalfont\normalsize\bfseries}{Preparations for power counting.}
We introduce the following abbreviations (for $\theta\in [0,1]$):
\begin{align*}
   B_\theta=\theta B,\qquad \mathrm{d}_\theta:=\mathrm{d}_{B_\theta},  \qquad R_\theta:=R_{B_\theta}(1+\lambda), \qquad H_\theta^s:=H_{B_\theta}^s.
\end{align*}
We also define $\tilde \Xi_0:= \{A,B,B^*B,A^*B,A^2\}$.
All these terms belong to $C^{-\kappa/2}$ or $\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}$ by Sobolev embedding and Young's multiplication theorem.\relax{Note that we are losing a lot of regularity for $B$ and $B^*B$ in doing so, but our argument does not need the better regularities.}

\@startsection{paragraph}{4}{\z@}{1.5ex \@plus .5ex \@minus .2ex}{-1em}{\normalfont\normalsize\bfseries}{Treatment ${\mathscr q}^1_{A,B}$.} We apply the power counting Lemma~\ref{lem:power_counting} directly to ${\mathscr q}^1_{\mathbf{A},B}(\lambda)=2R_B(1+\lambda) A^*\mathrm{d}_B R_B(1+\lambda)$. We count two resolvents and one derivative, giving
\begin{align}\label{eq:good_bound}
\nonumber |\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}_{A,B}^1(\lambda))|&\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa} (1+\lambda)^{2(-1+2\kappa)} (1+\lambda)^{\frac 1 2} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\kappa} (1+\|B\|)^{4\kappa} \|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}\\
&\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 1 2+2\kappa}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{6\kappa}\|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}.
\end{align}
This bound does not have enough decay in $\lambda$ for integrability. We next prove a bound with enough decay in $\lambda$ but super-quadratic in $B$, then interpolate between the two bounds.

To that end, define $X_\theta (\lambda):={\mathscr q}_{\mathbf{A},B_\theta}(\lambda)=2R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta$. The map $\theta\mapsto X_\theta (\lambda)$ is twice differentiable with continuous derivatives by Lemma~\ref{lem:differentiating_resolvents} and differentiability of $\theta\mapsto \mathrm{d}_\theta$. Lemma~\ref{lem:differentiation_trace} then gives
\begin{align}\label{eq:differentiating_q1}
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}_{A,B}^1(\lambda))&=\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^1_{A,0}(\lambda))+\operatorname{Tr}(\dot X_0(\lambda)) + \int_0^1 (1-\theta)\operatorname{Tr}(\ddot X_\theta(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\theta\\
&=\operatorname{Tr}(\dot X_0(\lambda)) + \int_0^1 (1-\theta)\operatorname{Tr}(\ddot X_\theta(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\theta,
\end{split}
\end{align}
where we have used $\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^1_{\mathbb{A},0}(\lambda))=0$ from~\eqref{eq:tr_q1_vanishes}.
We first compute
 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Xdot_definition}
    \dot X_\theta(\lambda)=-4R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta+2R_\theta A^*BR_\theta-4R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta.
    \end{equation}
    At $\theta=0$, taking the trace and using Proposition~\ref{prop:Pi_quadratic_form} gives
    \begin{align}
    \operatorname{Tr}(\dot X_0(\lambda))&=2\boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda(A,B),\nonumber\\
    |\operatorname{Tr}(\dot X_0(\lambda))|&\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 3 2 +\kappa}\|B\|_{H^1}\|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}.\label{eq:Xdot_bound}
    \end{align}

    Differentiating~\eqref{eq:Xdot_definition} once more gives
    \begin{align*}
  \ddot X_\theta(\lambda)&=8 R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta-4R_\theta B^*B R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta+8R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta \\
    &\quad -4R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*BR_\theta +8R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta \\
    &\quad -4R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*BR_\theta-4R_\theta A^*BR_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta \\
    &\quad +8R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta -4R_\theta A^*BR_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta +8 R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta \\
    &\quad -4R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*BR_\theta +8 R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta.
    \end{align*}
    This simplifies to
    \begin{align*}
    \ddot X_\theta(\lambda)    &=
16R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta
-4R_\theta B^*BR_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta
-8R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*BR_\theta
\\
&\quad
+16R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta
-8R_\theta A^*BR_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta
+16R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta
\\
&\quad
-4R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*BR_\theta.
    \end{align*}
The three terms with coefficient $16$ have three derivatives and $4$ resolvents, so power counting Lemma~\ref{lem:power_counting} gives the trace bound
\[
(1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa} (1+\lambda)^{4(-1+2\kappa)}(1+\lambda)^{3\cdot\frac 12} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{3\cdot 2\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{3\cdot 4\kappa} \|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}\|B\|_{H^1}^2.
\]
All other terms have $1$ derivative  and $3$ resolvents,  so the trace is bounded by
\[
(1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa} (1+\lambda)^{3(-1+2\kappa)} (1+\lambda)^{\frac 1 2} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\cdot 4\kappa} \|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}\|B\|_{H^1}^2.
\]
Hence we combine both estimates to get
\begin{align*}
\int_0^1 (1-\theta)|\operatorname{Tr}(\ddot X_\theta(\lambda))|\,\mathrm{d} \theta
\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac32+6\kappa}\|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{18\kappa}\|B\|_{H^1}^2.
\end{align*}
In particular, this bound together with~\eqref{eq:differentiating_q1} and~\eqref{eq:Xdot_bound} yields
\begin{align}\label{eq:bad_bound}
|\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^1_{A,B}(\lambda))|\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac32+6\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2+18\kappa} \|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}.
\end{align}

Finally, we interpolate~\eqref{eq:good_bound} and~\eqref{eq:bad_bound} to obtain \begin{align}\label{eq:Tr_q1_bound}
|\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^1_{A,B}(\lambda))|\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-1-2\kappa+24\kappa^2} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+24\kappa+72\kappa^2} \|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}.
\end{align}
For $\kappa<\frac 1 {12}$, the power of $\lambda$ is less than $-1$, so this bound is integrable in $\lambda$.  \@startsection{paragraph}{4}{\z@}{1.5ex \@plus .5ex \@minus .2ex}{-1em}{\normalfont\normalsize\bfseries}{Treatment of ${\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},B}$.} With the same abbreviations as above, we write using~Lemma~\ref{lem:differentiation_trace}
\begin{align}\label{eq:differentiating_q2}
\nonumber\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))-\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},0})&=\int_0^1 \operatorname{Tr}(\partial_\theta {\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},\theta B}(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d} \theta\\
&=\int_0^1 \operatorname{Tr}\big(\partial_\theta(R_\theta A^2 R_\theta)- 4\partial_\theta(R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}\theta BR_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta)\big)\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
\end{align}
 The first term is equal to
    \[
   \partial_{\theta}(R_{\theta}A^2 R_\theta)=-2R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^2 R_\theta-2R_\theta A^2R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta,
    \]
where each term on the right has $1$ derivative and $3$ resolvents, so Lemma~\ref{lem:power_counting} gives the trace bound
\[
(1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa}(1+\lambda)^{3(-1+2\kappa)}(1+\lambda)^{\frac 1 2}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\cdot 4\kappa} \|B\|\|A^2\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}.
\]

Regarding the second term in~\eqref{eq:differentiating_q2}, we find
\begin{align*}
    \partial_\theta (R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta) &=-2R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta +R_\theta A^* BR_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta \\
    &\qquad -2R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta +R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^* BR_\theta\\
    &\qquad -2R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta A^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta.
    \end{align*}
   The three terms with coefficient $-2$ have $3$ derivatives and $4$ resolvents, so their trace is bounded by
   \[
   (1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa}(1+\lambda)^{4(-1+2\kappa)}(1+\lambda)^{3\cdot\frac 1 2}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{3\cdot 2\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{3\cdot 4\kappa} \|B\|\|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}^2.
   \]
   The remaining terms have $1$ derivative and $3$ resolvents, so their trace is bounded by
    \[
   (1+\lambda)^{1-2\kappa}(1+\lambda)^{3(-1+2\kappa)}(1+\lambda)^{\frac 1 2}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\cdot 4\kappa} \|B\|\|A\|_{C^{-\kappa/2}}^2.
   \]
Combining all these estimates then yields
\begin{align}\label{eq:Tr_q2_bound}
|\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))-\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^2_{\mathbb{A},0})|\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-\frac 3 2 +6\kappa} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+18\kappa}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^2.
\end{align}
This is integrable in $\lambda$ for $\kappa<\frac 1{12}$.

\@startsection{paragraph}{4}{\z@}{1.5ex \@plus .5ex \@minus .2ex}{-1em}{\normalfont\normalsize\bfseries}{Treatment of ${\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}$.}

We have, with the second identity following from Lemma~\ref{lem:differentiation_trace},
\begin{gather*}
{\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)-\tilde{\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)
= (m_{\mathbb{A},B}-1)\big(R_B(1+\lambda)^2-R_0(1+\lambda)^2\big),\\
\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))-\operatorname{Tr}(\tilde{\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))
= (m_{\mathbb{A},B}-1)\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_\theta R_\theta^2)\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
\end{gather*}
We also have, by differentiation and cyclicity of the trace,
\begin{gather*}
\partial_\theta R_\theta^2
= -2R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta^2-2R_\theta^2B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta,\\
\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_\theta R_\theta^2)=-4\operatorname{Tr}(R_\theta B^*\mathrm{d}_\theta R_\theta^2).
\end{gather*}
The power counting Lemma~\ref{lem:power_counting} gives
\begin{align}\label{eq:difference_resolvents_trace}
\nonumber |\operatorname{Tr}(R_B(1+\lambda)^2-R_0(1+\lambda)^2)|&\leq \int_0^1|\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_\theta R_\theta^2)|\,\mathrm{d}\theta \\
&\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{-\frac32+4\kappa}
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{6\kappa}\|B\|_{H^1}.
\end{align}
Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:difference_masses},  using $m_{\0,B}=1$ gives
\[
|m_{\mathbb{A},B}-1|
\lesssim
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\frac{15\kappa}{1-3\kappa}}
(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{\frac{2}{1-3\kappa}}
{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
\]
Hence,
\begin{align}\label{eq:Tr_q3_bound}
&|\operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda)-\tilde{\mathscr q}^3_{\mathbb{A},B}(\lambda))|\lesssim
(1+\lambda)^{-\frac32+4\kappa}
(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+6\kappa+\frac{15\kappa}{1-3\kappa}}
(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{1+\frac{2}{1-3\kappa}}.
\end{align}
This is integrable in $\lambda$ for $\kappa<\frac1{8}$, hence in particular for $\kappa<\frac 1{12}$.

\@startsection{paragraph}{4}{\z@}{1.5ex \@plus .5ex \@minus .2ex}{-1em}{\normalfont\normalsize\bfseries}{Concluding the lower bound.}
For~\eqref{eq:Q_N_rewritten}, it remains to treat the terms with ${\mathscr q}^i_{\mathbb{A},B}$ for $i=1,2,3$. The bounds on their integrands in~\eqref{eq:Tr_q1_bound},\eqref{eq:Tr_q2_bound} and~\eqref{eq:Tr_q3_bound} show that each integral with ${\mathscr q}^i_{\mathbb{A},B}$ is bounded in absolute value by a multiple of $(1+{\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+\tau(\kappa)}$, uniformly in $N$. This finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition}
    Let $\kappa\in(0,\frac14)$, $\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ and $B\in\Omega^1H^1$.
    Denote $d=1+3\kappa$.
Then, for every $s<1-3\kappa$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cov_GFF_decomposition_difference}
\mathbb{E}\|\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}-\phi_{\bar\mathbb{A},B,N}\|_{H_B^s}^2
\lesssim
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)^4
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^2.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
By It\^o isometry,
\begin{align} \label{eq:cov_GFF_dec_proof_Ito}
\mathbb{E}\|\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N} &- \phi_{\bar\mathbb{A},B,N}\|_{H_B^s}^2= \nonumber\\
&2\int_0^N \| (L_B+1)^{s/2} (R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda))\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
\end{align}
Choose $\gamma>1$ so that
\[
\max\{0,s+1\}<s+\gamma<2-3\kappa.
\]
Then $\| (L_B+1)^{-\gamma/2}\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \lesssim 1$.
Writing $(L_B+1)^{s/2} = (L_B+1)^{-\gamma/2}(L_B+1)^{(s+\gamma)/2}$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
&\| (L_B+1)^{s/2} (R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda))\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
\\
&\leq \|(L_B+1)^{-\gamma /2}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
\|(R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda))\|_{L^2 \to H^{s+\gamma}_B}.
\end{align*}
Recall $d=1+3\kappa$. Since $s+\gamma<2-\kappa$, \eqref{eq:pushed_resolvent_difference} gives
\[
\|(R_{\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda)-R_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}(m_{\bar\mathbb{A},B}+\lambda))\|_{L^2 \to H^{s+\gamma}_B}
\lesssim
(\lambda+1)^{-\frac32 + \frac{3\kappa}{2} + \frac{s+\gamma}{2}}
{\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A};B)^2
{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar\mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa},
\]
from which \eqref{eq:cov_GFF_decomposition_difference} follows
provided that $-3 + 3\kappa + s+\gamma<-1
\Leftrightarrow s+\gamma<2-3\kappa$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:cov_GFF_finite_cutoff}
    In the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition}, one has for any $0<s<1-3\kappa$
    \[
    \mathbb{E}\|\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}\|_{H^s_B}^2
    \lesssim
    N^{1-3\kappa}
    +
    {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)^4
    {\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^2.
