    \]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Set $\gamma:=2-3\kappa-s>1$, and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:neg_power_trace} and Lemma~\ref{lem:resolvent_estimate_classical}, to obtain
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E} \|\phi_{\0,B,N}\|_{H^s_B}^2
&=
2\int_0^N \|(L_B+1)^{s/2}R_B(1+\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
\\
&\leq 2\int_0^N \|(L_B+1)^{-\gamma/2}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 \|(L_B+1)^{(s+\gamma)/2}R_B(1+\lambda)\|_{L^2\to L^2}^2\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
\\
&\lesssim \int_0^N (1+\lambda)^{-2+s+\gamma}\,\mathrm{d}\lambda \; \lesssim N^{1-3\kappa}.
\end{align*}
Combining this estimate with Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition} yields the result.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:Wick_prods}
Let $\zeta$ be a centred circular complex Gaussian, and define ${\mathrm{z}}:=\mathbb{E}[|\zeta|^2]$.
Then, for any $\eta\in\mathbb{C}$ and any integer $k\ge0$, the Wick power with respect to the base ${\mathrm{z}}$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:def_Wick_power}
\llbracket |\eta|^{2k} \rrbracket=\sum_{j=0}^{k}(-1)^j\binom kj^2 j!\,{\mathrm{z}}^{\,j}\,|\eta|^{2(k-j)}=|\eta|^{2k}-\sum_{l=0}^{k-1}{\mathrm{v}}^{(k)}_l({\mathrm{z}})\,|\eta|^{2l},
\end{equation}

Moreover, we have the following.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\par\hangindent 40\p@\label{item:Wick_monomials} For all integers $i,j\ge0$,
\begin{align*}
\llbracket \zeta^{i}(\zeta^*)^{j} \rrbracket=\sum_{r=0}^{i\wedge j}(-1)^r\binom ir\binom jr\,r!\,{\mathrm{z}}^{\,r}\,\zeta^{\,i-r}(\zeta^*)^{\,j-r}.
\end{align*}
In particular $\llbracket \zeta^{i} \rrbracket=\zeta^{i}$ and $\llbracket (\zeta^*)^{j} \rrbracket=(\zeta^*)^{j}$, moreover $\big(\llbracket \zeta^{i}(\zeta^*)^{j} \rrbracket\big)^*=\llbracket \zeta^{j}(\zeta^*)^{i} \rrbracket$, and $\mathbb{E}\big[\llbracket \zeta^{i}(\zeta^*)^{j} \rrbracket\big]=0$ unless $i=j=0$.
\par\hangindent 40\p@\label{item:Wick_shift} For every integer $k\ge0$ and every $w\in\mathbb{C}$,
\begin{align*}
|\zeta+w|^{2k}-\sum_{l=0}^{k-1}{\mathrm{v}}^{(k)}_l({\mathrm{z}})\,|\zeta+w|^{2l}=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom ki\binom kj\,\llbracket \zeta^{i}(\zeta^*)^{j} \rrbracket\,w^{\,k-i}(w^*)^{\,k-j},
\end{align*}
equivalently, in real form,
\begin{align*}
\llbracket |\zeta+w|^{2k} \rrbracket=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\binom ki^2\llbracket |\zeta|^{2i} \rrbracket\,|w|^{2(k-i)}+2\mathfrak{Re}\sum_{0\le j<i\le k}\binom ki\binom kj\,\llbracket \zeta^{i}(\zeta^*)^{j} \rrbracket\,w^{\,k-i}(w^*)^{\,k-j}.
\end{align*}
\par\hangindent 40\p@\label{item:Wick_V} Consequently, for $\mathcal{V}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}c_kx^k$ and with ${\mathrm{v}}_l$ as in~\eqref{eq:def_counterterm_family} below,
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{V}(|\zeta+w|^2)-\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}{\mathrm{v}}_l({\mathrm{z}})\,|\zeta+w|^{2l}
=\sum_{k=0}^{n}c_k\sum_{i,j=0}^{k}\binom ki\binom kj\,\llbracket \zeta^{i}(\zeta^*)^{j} \rrbracket\,w^{\,k-i}(w^*)^{\,k-j}.
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:wick-powers}
  Let $i,j\geq0$, $p,q\in[1,\infty)$ and $\varepsilon,\eta>0$.  Uniformly in
  $N$ and in Coulomb-gauge $B\in H^1$,
  \[
    \mathbb E\!\left[
      \bigl\|\llbracket\phi_{0,B,N}^{i}
      (\phi_{0,B,N}^{\ast})^{j}\rrbracket_N
      \bigr\|_{W^{-\varepsilon,p}}^q
    \right]^{1/q}
    \leq C(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\eta}.
  \]
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:wickmoment}
For every $\delta>0$, $p\in[1,\infty)$ and $q\in[1,\infty)$, and $i,j \in \mathbb{N}$,
\[
\sup_{N>0}\ \sup_{B\in\Omega^1H^1}\ \mathbb{E}\Big[\big\|\llbracket \phi_{\0,B,N}^{\,i}(\phi_{\0,B,N}^{*})^{j} \rrbracket_{B,N}\big\|^{q}_{W^{-\delta,p}}\Big]<\infty\;.
\]
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Let $B\in\Omega^1_\mathrm{C} H^1$ and $N>0$. For almost every $(x,y)\in\mathbb{T}^2\times\mathbb{T}^2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:diamagnetic} gives $|R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y)|\le R_0(1+\lambda)(x-y)$; since $R_0(1+\lambda)\ge0$, composing kernels preserves the domination, so $|R_B(1+\lambda)^2(x,y)|\le R_0(1+\lambda)^2(x-y)$, and~\eqref{eq:cov_kernel_phi} gives
\[
\big|C_{B,N}(x,y)\big|\le2\int_0^N R_0(1+\lambda)^2(x-y)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:semi-group} with $\gamma=2$ gives $R_0(1+\lambda)^2=\int_0^\infty te^{-(1+\lambda)t}p_t\,\mathrm{d} t$, and $\int_0^N e^{-\lambda t}\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\le t^{-1}$, so that
\[
\int_0^N R_0(1+\lambda)^2(z)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\le\int_0^\infty te^{-t}t^{-1}p_t(z)\,\mathrm{d} t=R_0(1)(z),
\]
uniformly in $N$. Hence
\[
\big|C_{B,N}(x,y)\big|\le 2R_0(1)(x-y)\lesssim 1+\log\frac1{|x-y|}.
\]
Moreover, the standard two-dimensional massive Green's function estimates give $R_0(1)\in L^\rho(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for every $\rho<\infty$, with
$
\|R_0(1)\|_{L^\rho}\lesssim\rho.
$
All these bounds are uniform in $B$ and $N$.

The moment bounds then follow from standard Gaussian estimates combined with the kernel domination established above.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:comp_renorm_constants}
Let $B\in\Omega^1_\mathrm{C} H^1$ and  $j\ge1$ be an integer. For any $s\in[0,1)$ and $q\in(1,\infty)$ with $sq<1$, and any $\delta_0\in(s,1)$,
\[
\big\|\hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}^{\,j}\big\|_{W^{s,q}}\lesssim_{j,s,q,\delta_0}(1+\|B\|_{\Omega^1H^1})^{j\delta_0},
\]
where the implicit constant is independent of $N$ and of $B$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We write
\[
\hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}(x)=2\int_0^N a_\lambda(x) \,\mathrm{d} \lambda, \qquad a_\lambda(x):=R_B(1+\lambda)^2(x,x)-R_0(1+\lambda)^2(x,x).
\]
We derive an $L^\infty$ bound for $a_\lambda$ and a $B^\varepsilon_{r,1}$ bound for $\mathrm{d} a_\lambda$, then interpolate.

For the $L^\infty$ bound, we use diamagnetic inequality Lemmas~\ref{lem:diamagnetic} and~\ref{lem:neg_power_trace}, to obtain
\begin{align}\label{eq:L_infty_bound_a_lambda}
\|a_\lambda\|_{L^\infty}\leq 2R_0(1+\lambda)^2(0) =2\operatorname{Tr}(R_0(1+\lambda)^2)\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-1}.
\end{align}
Note that
\[
\langle \hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N},1\rangle=2\int_0^N \operatorname{Tr}(R_B(1+\lambda)^2-R_0(1+\lambda)^2)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
\]
Then interpolating the $L^\infty$ bound~\eqref{eq:L_infty_bound_a_lambda} and~\eqref{eq:difference_resolvents_trace}, we get
\[
|\langle \hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N},1\rangle|\lesssim_\varepsilon (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^\varepsilon.
\]
Regarding the derivative, we use self-adjointness  $R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y)^*=R_B(1+\lambda)(y,x)$ to write
\begin{align*}
\partial_{x_i} a_\lambda(x)&=\partial_{x_i} \int R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y) R_B(1+\lambda)(y,x)\,\mathrm{d} y\\
&=\partial_{x_i} \int |R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y)|^2\,\mathrm{d} y\\
&=2\mathfrak{Re} \int \partial_{x_i}  R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y) R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y)^* \,\mathrm{d} y.
\end{align*}
Since $B$ is purely imaginary we can make the derivative a covariant derivative so that
\[
\partial_{x_i} a_\lambda(x)=2\mathfrak{Re} \int (\partial_{x_i}+B_i(x)) R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y) R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y)^* \,\mathrm{d} y.
\]
In particular for a real-valued $1$-form $K\in\Omega^1 C^\infty$
\begin{align*}
\langle K,\mathrm{d} a_\lambda\rangle&=2\sum_{i=1}^2 \int K_i(x) \mathfrak{Re} \int (\partial_{x_i}+B_i(x)) R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y) R_B(1+\lambda)(x,y)^* \,\mathrm{d} y \,\mathrm{d} x\\
&=2 \mathfrak{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(K^* \mathrm{d}_B R_B(1+\lambda)^2).
\end{align*}
Thus
\[
\langle K,\mathrm{d} a_\lambda\rangle=\mathfrak{Re} \operatorname{Tr}({\mathscr q}^1_{K,B}(\lambda)),
\]
where ${\mathscr q}^1$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:def_q1}. Applying~\eqref{eq:Tr_q1_bound}, with $\kappa>0$ replaced by $\varepsilon>0$, gives
\[
|\langle K,\mathrm{d} a_\lambda\rangle|\lesssim_{\varepsilon} \|K\|_{C^{-\varepsilon}} (1+\lambda)^{-1-\gamma_\varepsilon} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+\beta_\varepsilon},
\]
with $\beta_\varepsilon,\gamma_\varepsilon>0$ such that $\beta_\varepsilon,\gamma_\varepsilon\to 0$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$.  Hence, by  Besov duality (see e.g.~\cite[Sec.~2.11.2]{Triebel})
\[
\|\mathrm{d} a_\lambda\|_{B^\varepsilon_{1,1}}\lesssim_\varepsilon (1+\lambda)^{-1-\gamma_\varepsilon} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+\beta_\varepsilon}.
\]
By Poincar\'e inequality, we get
\[
\|a_\lambda-\bar a_\lambda\|_{B^{1+\varepsilon}_{1,1}}\lesssim_{\varepsilon}  (1+\lambda)^{-1-\gamma_\varepsilon} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{1+\beta_\varepsilon}.
\]
where $\bar a_\lambda$ is the spatial mean of $a_\lambda$. Interpolating this with~\eqref{eq:L_infty_bound_a_lambda} (see e.g.~\cite[Sec.~2.4.7]{Triebel}) we get
\[
\|a_\lambda-\bar a_\lambda\|_{B^{(1+\varepsilon)/r}_{r,r}}\lesssim_{\varepsilon,r}  (1+\lambda)^{-1-\gamma_\varepsilon/r} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{(1+\beta_\varepsilon)/r}, \qquad r\geq 1.
\]

Choose $\varepsilon>0$ small enough such that we can find $r$ such that
\[
\max\Big\{q ,\frac{1+\beta_\varepsilon}{\delta_0}\Big\} <r<\frac{1+\varepsilon}{s}.
\]
Now set
\[
\alpha=\frac{1+\varepsilon}{r},
\]
which by assumption on $r$ implies $s<\alpha$, and since $r>q $, the Besov embedding $B^\alpha_{r,r}\subset W^{s,q }$ (see e.g.~\cite[Sec.~2.3.2]{Triebel}), yields
\[
\|a_\lambda-\bar a_\lambda\|_{W^{s,q }}\lesssim_{s,q ,\varepsilon,r}  (1+\lambda)^{-1-\gamma_\varepsilon/r} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{(1+\beta_\varepsilon)/r}.
\]

This bound gives a uniformly bounded integral in $\lambda$ for any sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, and
\begin{align*}
\|\hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}\|_{W^{s,q }}&\leq |\langle \hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N},1\rangle|+\Big\| \int_0^N a_\lambda-\bar a_\lambda\,\mathrm{d}\lambda  \Big\|_{W^{s,q }} \\
&\leq |\langle \hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N},1\rangle|+\int_0^N \|a_\lambda-\bar a_\lambda\|_{W^{s,q }}\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\\
&\lesssim_{s,q ,\varepsilon,r} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^\varepsilon+  (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\frac{1+\beta_\varepsilon}{r}}.
\end{align*}
Since $1+\beta_\varepsilon<r\delta_0$ by the choice of $r$, taking $\varepsilon>0$ smaller if necessary gives
\[
\|\hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}\|_{W^{s,q }}\lesssim_{s,q ,\delta_0} (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\delta_0}.
\]

For $j\ge2$ choose $q _2\in(q ,\infty)$ with $sq _2<1$, which is possible since $sq <1$, and let $q _1\in(1,\infty)$ be defined by $\frac{j-1}{q _1}=\frac1q -\frac1{q _2}$. The fractional product rule (see e.g.~\cite{BookChemin}) applied $j-1$ times gives
\[
\big\|\hat{\mathrm{p}}^{\,j}_{B,N}\big\|_{W^{s,q }}\lesssim\big\|\hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}\big\|^{j-1}_{L^{q _1}}\big\|\hat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}\big\|_{W^{s,q _2}},
\]
and we can conclude by applying the case $j=1$ twice: with $(s,q )=(0,q _1)$ to the first factor, and with $p=q _2$ to the second.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:change_base}
  \[
  \llbracket\phi_{\0,B,N}^i(\phi_{\0,B,N}^*)^j\rrbracket_N
    =\sum_{a=0}^{i\wedge j}\binom ia\binom ja a!\,
      \widehat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}^{a}
      \llbracket\phi_{\0,B,N}^{i-a}(\phi_{\0,B,N}^*)^{j-a}\rrbracket_{B,N}.
  \]
  The covariance-matched Wick products have moments bounded uniformly in
  $B$ and $N$ in every negative Sobolev space, by the diamagnetic covariance
  bound.  Moreover, for arbitrarily small $\eta_0>0$,
  Lemma~\ref{lem:comp_renorm_constants} gives
  \[
    \|\widehat{\mathrm{p}}_{B,N}^{a}\|_{W^{t,\sigma}}
      \lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{a\eta_0}
  \]
  for any $\sigma\in(1,\infty)$ and $t\in(0,\eta_0)$ with $t\sigma<1$.  Applying the
  product rule to each summand and choosing $\eta_0<\eta/(i\wedge j\vee1)$
  proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:drift_estimate}
 Let $\kappa\in(0,\frac14)$, $\mathbb{A}\in\mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$ and $B\in\Omega^1H^1$.  For any  $u\in\mathbb{H}^{\Phi}$ one has
\[
 \| I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}(u)\|_{H^{1-\nicefrac{\kappa}{2}}_B}
 \lesssim
 {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)^{1/2}
 \|u\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Let $f\in L^2$ and $u\in\mathbb{H}^\Phi$, and note that
    \begin{align*}
    \langle I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}(u),f\rangle&=\int_0^N \langle \Sigma_t^{\mathbb{A},B}u_t,f\rangle_{L^2}\,\mathrm{d} t=\int_0^N \langle u_t,\Sigma_t^{\mathbb{A},B}f\rangle\,\mathrm{d} t.
    \end{align*}
    Define $U:L^2\to \mathbb{H}^\Phi$ by
    \[
    (Uf)_t= \Sigma^{\mathbb{A},B}_t  f,
    \]
    and note that $U^*=I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}$.     Then we have that
    \[
    \int_0^N \|(Uf)_t\|_{L^2}^2\,\mathrm{d} t=\int_0^N \|\Sigma_t^{\mathbb{A},B} f\|_{L^2}^2\,\mathrm{d} t.
    \]
    Note that
    \begin{align*}
   \|\Sigma_t^{\mathbb{A},B} f\|_{L^2}&=\|(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B}+t)^{-1}f\|_{L^2}\leq (1+t)^{-1} \|f\|_{L^2}.
    \end{align*}
    Then
    \[
    \| Uf\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}^2=\|f\|_{L^2}^2 \int_0^N (1+t)^{-2}\,\mathrm{d} t  \leq \|f\|_{L^2}^2.
    \]
    If we now take $f=(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2}v$, we get
    \[
    \|U (L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2}v\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}\leq \|(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2}v\|_{L^2}.
    \]
    In particular, $U(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2}:{\mathscr{D}}((L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2})\to \mathbb{H}^\Phi$ is bounded and so is its adjoint, namely
    \[
    (U(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2})^*=(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2} I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}: \mathbb{H}^\Phi\to {\mathscr{D}}((L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2}),
    \]
    and
    \[
    \|(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2} I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}(u)\|_{L^2}\leq \|u\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}.
    \]
    Using~Corollary~\ref{cor:fractional_power_comparison_LAB} with $\theta=\frac12$, we obtain
    \[
    \| I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}(u)\|_{H^{1-\nicefrac{\kappa}{2}}_B}
    \lesssim
    {\mathfrak C}_\kappa(\mathbb{A};B)^{1/2}
    \|(L_{\mathbb{A},B}+m_{\mathbb{A},B})^{1/2} I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}(u)\|_{L^2},
    \]
    and hence the result follows.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:coercive-bound-higgs}
  Let $n\geq2$, $s\in(s_n,1)$, and let $P(z,z^*)$ be a homogeneous
  polynomial of total degree $1\leq r\leq2n-1$.  For every
  $\delta,\eta>0$ there are $\varepsilon>0$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $K<\infty$
  and $C<\infty$ such that, for $B\in H^1$, $f\in W^{-\varepsilon,p}$ and
  $Z\in H_B^s\cap L^{2n}$,
  \[
    \left|\int_{\mathbb{T}^2} fP(Z,Z^*)\ \right|
    \leq C\bigl(1+\|f\|_{W^{-\varepsilon,p}}^K\bigr)
      +\delta\|B\|_{H^1}^{\eta}
      +\delta\|Z\|_{H_B^s}^{3/2}
      +\delta\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n}.
  \]
  The constants are uniform in $B$ and $Z$; $C$ may depend on the
  coefficients of $P$.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
It is enough to treat a monomial.  If $r=1$, Sobolev duality and comparison
  of the flat and covariant norms give
  \[
    \left|\int fP(Z,Z^*)\right|
      \lesssim \|f\|_{H^{-\varepsilon}}
      (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^\varepsilon\|Z\|_{H_B^s},
  \]
  and the claim follows from Young's inequality after taking
  $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small.

  Let $2\leq r\leq2n-1$ and put $\lambda=2\varepsilon/s$.  Interpolation
  between $L^{2n}$ and $H^s$, followed by the fractional product rule, yields
  \[
    \|P(Z,Z^*)\|_{W^{\varepsilon,p'}}
    \lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{2\varepsilon}
      \|Z\|_{H_B^s}^{\lambda}\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{r-\lambda},
  \]
  where
  \[
    \frac1p=\frac{2n-r}{2n}-\frac{\varepsilon(n-1)}{sn}.
  \]
  For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, $p\in(1,\infty)$ and
  \[
    1-\frac{2\lambda}{3}-\frac{r-\lambda}{2n}>0.
  \]
  Duality and Young's inequality now give the asserted estimate.  Since all
  resulting powers of $\|B\|_{H^1}$ are $O_n(\varepsilon)$, they are at most
  $\eta$ after decreasing $\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:potential-bound-higgs}
  Let $\mathcal V(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n c_kx^k$, where $n\geq2$ and $c_n>0$.
  Let $s\in(s_n,1)$ and let $Z$ be an $H_B^s$-valued random variable, not
  necessarily independent of $\phi_{0,B,N}$.  For every $a_0,\delta,\eta>0$
  there are $C,K<\infty$ such that, uniformly in $N$, $a\geq a_0$ and
  $m\in\mathbb R$,
  \begin{align*}
    a\mathbb E {\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{0,B,N}+Z)
    &\leq C(a^K+|m|^K+1)+\delta\|B\|_{H^1}^{\eta}\\
    &\quad+\delta\mathbb E\|Z\|_{H_B^s}^{3/2}
      +C(a+\delta)\mathbb E\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n},\\
    a\mathbb E {\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{0,B,N}+Z)
    &\geq-C(a^K+|m|^K+1)-\delta\|B\|_{H^1}^{\eta}
      -\delta\mathbb E\|Z\|_{H_B^s}^{3/2}.
  \end{align*}
  Here $C$ depends on $a_0$, $\delta$, $\eta$ and the coefficients of
  $\mathcal V$, but not on $a,m,B,N$ or $Z$.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Put $\phi=\phi_{0,B,N}$.  For every $k$ the exact shifted Wick expansion is
  \[
    \llbracket|\phi+Z|^{2k}\rrbracket_N
    =\sum_{i,j=0}^k\binom ki\binom kj
      \llbracket\phi^i(\phi^*)^j\rrbracket_N
      Z^{k-i}(Z^*)^{k-j}.
  \]
  Terms of $Z$-degree between $1$ and $2n-1$ are controlled by
  Lemmas~\ref{lem:coercive-bound-higgs} and~\ref{lem:wick-powers}.  The
  $Z$-free terms are controlled directly by Lemma~\ref{lem:wick-powers}; the
  pure powers of degree below $2n$ are controlled by H\"older and Young.
  The remaining pure term is $ac_n\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n}$.

  Finally,
  \[
    |\phi+Z|^2-{\mathrm{p}}_N
      =\llbracket|\phi|^2\rrbracket_N
       +2\operatorname{Re}(\phi^*Z)+|Z|^2,
  \]
  so the same estimates cover the linear and $Z$-free mass terms,
  while the quadratic term is bounded by a small multiple of
  $\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n}$ plus $C(a^K+|m|^K+1)$.  For the lower bound, all small
  $L^{2n}$ terms are absorbed by $ac_n\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n}$, uniformly
  for $a\geq a_0$.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:higgs-W-bound}
  Assume $|h(A,\psi)|\leq c(1+\|A\|^{2}_{C^{-\eta}}+\|\psi\|^{2n}_{C^{-\eta}})$  for some $\eta_0>0$ $c=c(n,\eta)>0$ sufficiently small and let $q\geq1$, $m\in\mathbb R$, and let
  $0<\kappa<1/(4n)$.  Then there are $K<\infty$ and $\tau(\kappa)>0$ (as usual $\tau(\kappa)\to0$ as $\kappa\to0$) such
  that, for every $\delta>0$, uniformly in $N$ and in Coulomb-gauge
  $B\in H^1$,
  \[
    \mathcal W_N^{h,q,m}(\mathbb A,B)
    \geq-C\bigl(q+\|\mathbb A\|_{-\kappa}+1+|m|\bigr)^K
      -\delta\|B\|_{H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)}-c\|A\|_{H^{-\eta}},
  \]
  and
  \[
    \mathcal W_N^{h,q,m}(\mathbb A,0)
    \leq C\bigl(q+\|\mathbb A\|_{-\kappa}+1+|m|\bigr)^K+\|A\|_{H^{-\eta}}.
  \]
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
The Bou\'e--Dupuis formula reads
  \[
    \mathcal W_N^{h,q,m}(\mathbb A,B)
    =\inf_{u\in\mathbb H_a^{ \Phi  }}\mathbb E\!\left[
      -qh(A,\phi_{0,B,N}+Z)+q{\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{0,B,N}+Z)
      +\frac12\|u\|_{\mathbb H^{ \Phi  }}^2\right],
  \]
  where
  \[
    Z=I_N^{\mathbb A,B}(u)+\phi_{\mathbb A,B,N}-\phi_{0,B,N}.
  \]
  Choose $s\in(s_n,1-4\kappa)$.  The drift estimate Lemma~\ref{lem:drift_estimate} and the covariant GFF
  decomposition Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition} imply, for some finite powers depending only on $\kappa$,
  \[
    \mathbb E\|Z\|_{H_B^s}^{3/2}
      \leq C((1+\|\mathbb A\|_{-\kappa})^K+\|B\|_{H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)})
        +\varepsilon\mathbb E\|u\|_{\mathbb H^{ \Phi  }}^2.
  \]
  Lemma~\ref{lem:potential-bound-higgs} with $a=q$, together with the growth
  bound on $h$, gives the lower estimate after choosing $\varepsilon$ small
  enough to absorb the drift cost into the entropy term.

  For the upper estimate set $B=0$ and $u=0$.  Then $Z$ is Gaussian, and
  Gaussian moment equivalence, the embedding $H^s\subset L^{2n}$, and the
  covariant GFF decomposition give
  \[
    \mathbb E\|Z\|_{H^s}^{3/2}
      +\mathbb E\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n}
      \leq C(1+\|\mathbb A\|_{-\kappa})^K.
  \]
  Applying the upper estimate of Lemma~\ref{lem:potential-bound-higgs} and
  the growth bound on $h$ completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
The upper bound is stated only at $B=0$, which is all the construction requires: in the outer variational problem of \S\ref{sec:construction_measure} the upper bound on $\mathcal{W}$ enters only through the choice of drift $v=0$ (equivalently $B_T=J_T(0)=0$), while a nonzero drift $B_T=J_T(v)$ is controlled by the lower bound above, valid for all $B\in\Omega^1H^1$ with $\mathrm{d}^*B=0$.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:higgs_convergence}
Let $\kappa\in (0,\kappa_0)$, $\mathbb{A},\bar\mathbb{A} \in \mathcal{X}^{-\kappa}$, and $B\in\Omega^1 H^1$. Further define $m\coloneqq m_{\mathbb{A},B}$ and $\bar m\coloneqq m_{\bar \mathbb{A},B}$. Then the following limit exists
    \[
    \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m}(\mathbb{A},B) =: \mathcal{W}_\infty^{h,1,m}(\mathbb{A},B).
    \]
Furthermore, there exist exponents $\tau(\kappa)$ and ${\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)$ such that, for all $N\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$,
	\[
	|\mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m}(\mathbb{A},B)-\mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,\bar m}(\bar \mathbb{A},B)| \lesssim (1+\|B\|_{\Omega^1 H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)} {\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
	\]
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
For the first part of the theorem, we argue as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:potential-bound-higgs}. Let $\phi_N := \phi_{0,B,N}$ and $Z_N := \phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}-\phi_{0,B,N}$. ${\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})={\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_N + Z_N)$ is a continuous function of the complex Wick powers of $\phi_N$ (up to degree $2n$) in the $\llbracket \cdot \rrbracket_N$-ordering and $Z_N,Z_N^*$, each viewed as elements of their respective negative and positive regularity Sobolev spaces. We claim that the former converge in probability as $N\to\infty$ in the corresponding Wiener chaos generated by $X^ \Phi  $, and the latter converge in $L^2(\mathbb{P}^ \Phi  )$ as random functions in $H^s_B$ for $0<s<1$.

Indeed, we see from the formula in \eqref{eq:change_base} that any monomial $\llbracket \phi_N^i(\phi_N^*) \rrbracket_N$ is a linear combination of monomials ordered in $\llbracket \cdot \rrbracket_{N,B}$ paired with integer powers of the deterministic function $\hat p_{B,N}$. The $\llbracket \cdot \rrbracket_{N,B}$-ordered Wick powers converge in probability by standard Wiener chaos results, and the deterministic functions converge in $W^{t,\sigma}$ for small enough (positive) $t$ and $\sigma$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:comp_renorm_constants} and the fractional product rule.

The $L^2$ convergence of $Z_N$ can be deduced from Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition} by observing that the representation in \eqref{eq:cov_GFF_dec_proof_Ito}, in combination with the $L^1(\mathrm{d} \lambda)$-integrable bounds shown thereafter, easily yields that the sequence $(Z_N)_{N\ge 0}$ is Cauchy.

The test function $h$ is continuous by assumption and so is the (real) exponential function. We conclude that the random variables
\[
e^{-h(A,\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}) + {\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})}
\]
converge in law as $N\to\infty$. Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs-W-bound} for any $q>1$ implies that these random variables are also uniformly integrable, and so it follows that the limit
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E}[e^{-h(A,\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}) + {\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})}]=\mathbb{E}[\lim_{N\to\infty} e^{-h(\phi_{A,\mathbb{A},B,N}) + {\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})}]
\]
exists. Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs-W-bound} further shows that it is bounded away from $0$ and infinity, and hence the limiting free energy $\mathcal{W}_\infty^{h,1,m}(\mathbb{A},B)$ exists as a real number.

The second part of the theorem will follow if we prove local Lipschitz bounds uniformly in $N$. For simplicity, we set $h=0$. Extending the result to continuous test functions with suitably controlled growth is not difficult. We introduce the shorthand notation
\[
\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta := (1-\beta){\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}) + \beta {\mathscr{V}}_N^{\bar m}(\phi_{\bar \mathbb{A},B,N}),
\]
and we write the difference of free energies as
\begin{equation} \label{eq:Higgs_convergence_proof_free_energy_diff}
\mathcal{W}_N^{0,1,m}(\mathbb{A},B)-\mathcal{W}_N^{0,1,\bar m}(\bar \mathbb{A},B) = \int_0^1\;\frac{\mathbb{E}\Big[\big({\mathscr{V}}_N^{\bar m}(\phi_{\bar \mathbb{A},B,N})-{\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})\big)e^{-\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\Big]}{\mathbb{E}\big[e^{-\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big]}\,\,\mathrm{d} \beta.
\end{equation}
Differentiating under the expectation can be verified by adapting the next following arguments. We thus omit the details. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:potential-bound-higgs} to
\[
{\mathscr{V}}_N^m\big(\phi_{0,B,N}+(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}-\phi_{0,B,N}+I_N^{\mathbb{A},B}(u))\big)
\]
and
\[
{\mathscr{V}}_N^{\bar m}\big(\phi_{0,B,N}+(\phi_{\bar \mathbb{A},B,N}-\phi_{0,B,N}+I_N^{\bar \mathbb{A},B}(u))\big)
\]
separately, we infer upper and lower bounds for $-\log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-q\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big]$, for any $q\ge 1$, in terms of convex combinations of the bounds provided by Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs-W-bound}. Given any exponent $1<q\le 2$, convexity of the free energy gives
\[
\log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-q\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big] \le (2-q)\log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big] + (q-1) \log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-2\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big]
\]
and hence (for $K$ and $\delta$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs-W-bound})
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{q}\log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-q\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big]-\log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big] &\le \frac{q-1}{q}\Big(\log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-2\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big]+2\log \mathbb{E}\big[e^{-\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big]\Big) \\
&\lesssim (q-1)\big(6+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+|m|+{\vvvert \bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+|\bar m|\big)^K \\
&\quad\quad +(q-1)\delta\|B\|_{H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)} =: (q-1)M(\mathbb{A},\bar \mathbb{A},B).
\end{align*}
We recall the bounds on the masses $m$ and $\bar m$ implied by Lemma~\ref{lem:difference_masses}. $M(\mathbb{A},\bar \mathbb{A},B)$ raised to any power will therefore give an acceptable upper bound in view of our claim. Now apply H\"older's inequality with $q=1+M(\mathbb{A},\bar \mathbb{A},B)^{-1}$ in \eqref{eq:Higgs_convergence_proof_free_energy_diff} to find that
\[
\frac{\Big|\mathbb{E}\Big[\big({\mathscr{V}}_N^{\bar m}(\phi_{\bar \mathbb{A},B,N})-{\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})\big)e^{-\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\Big]\Big|}{\mathbb{E}\big[e^{-\tilde {\mathscr{V}}_\beta}\big]} \lesssim \mathbb{E}[|{\mathscr{V}}_N^{\bar m}(\phi_{\bar \mathbb{A},B,N})-{\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})|^p]^{1/p}
\]
with $p=M(\mathbb{A},\bar \mathbb{A},B)$. The proof therefore reduces to showing the next lemma.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
For any $p\ge 2$, there exist $\tau(\kappa)$ and $K_1,K_2>0$ such that
\[
\|{\mathscr{V}}_N^{\bar m}(\phi_{\bar \mathbb{A},B,N})-{\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})\|_{L^p(\mathbb{P}^ \Phi  )} \lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}p^{K_1}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{K_2}{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
As before, write $\phi:= \phi_{0,B,N}$, $Z_{\mathbb{A}}:=\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N}-\phi_{0,B,N}$ and likewise for $Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}}$. A generic term in the difference ${\mathscr{V}}_N^{\bar m}(\phi_{\bar \mathbb{A},B,N})-{\mathscr{V}}_N^m(\phi_{\mathbb{A},B,N})$ takes the form
\[
\mathcal{T} := \int_{\mathbb{T}^2}\; \llbracket \phi^i(\phi^*)^j \rrbracket_N \hat Z P(Z_{\mathbb{A}},Z_{\mathbb{A}}^*,Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}},Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}}^*)\,\mathrm{d} x,
\]
where $0\le i,j\le n$, $\hat Z$ stands for $Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}} - Z_{\mathbb{A}}$ or $Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}}^* - Z_{\mathbb{A}}^*$, and $P$ is some homogeneous polynomial of degree $2n-i-j-1$. For the degree two terms, factors of $m$, $\bar m$ or $\bar m -m$ may also appear. We argue as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:coercive-bound-higgs}, save that we are not concerned about exploiting the coercivity of the potential. We have for any $\varepsilon>0$ and H\"older conjugates $q,q'$,
\[
|\mathcal{T}|\le \|\llbracket \phi^i(\phi^*)^j \rrbracket_N\|_{W^{-\varepsilon,q}}\|\hat Z P(Z_{\mathbb{A}},Z_{\mathbb{A}}^*,Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}},Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}}^*)\|_{W^{\varepsilon,q'}},
\]
up to any additional factors involving the masses $\bar m$ and $m$. After applying the fractional product rule, we bound the factor with positive regularity by
\[
\|Z\|_{W^{\varepsilon,\tilde q}} \lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\varepsilon}\|Z\|_{H^s_B}
\]
for $s>\varepsilon +1-2/\tilde q$ (which follows by suitable interpolation as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:coercive-bound-higgs}), and all remaining factors by the diamagnetic embedding
\[
\|Z\|_{L^{2n}} \lesssim \|Z\|_{H^s_B}
\]
for $s>1-1/n$. There is also a term where $\hat Z$ is replaced by $\bar m-m$, for which Lemma~\ref{lem:difference_masses} supplies an adequate estimate. We thus arrive at a bound of the form
\begin{align*}
|\mathcal{T}| &\lesssim (1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^K\|\llbracket \phi^i(\phi^*)^j \rrbracket_N\|_{W^{-\varepsilon,q}} \times \\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad (\|\hat Z\|_{H^s_B}+{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})(\|Z_{\mathbb{A}}\|_{H^s_B}+\|Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}}\|_{H^s_B})^{2n-1}
\end{align*}
for small enough $\varepsilon$ and large enough $q$, $K$ (such that choosing $s<1$ is permitted), in which any possible mass dependence is already accounted for. We now take expectation, apply H\"older's inequality (with any distribution of finite exponents) and use the estimates provided by Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition} and Lemma~\ref{lem:wick-powers}. By Gaussian hypercontractivity (for any $r>2$), we obtain the bounds
\begin{align*}
\|\|\hat Z\|_{H^s_B}\|_{L^r(\mathbb{P}^ \Phi  )} &\lesssim r^{1/2} \|\|\hat Z\|_{H^s_B}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{P}^ \Phi  )} \\
&\lesssim r^{1/2}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}{\vvvert \mathbb{A}-\bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\|\|Z_{\mathbb{A}}\|_{H^s_B}\|_{L^r(\mathbb{P}^ \Phi  )} &, \|\|Z_{\bar \mathbb{A}}\|_{H^s_B}\|_{L^r(\mathbb{P}^ \Phi  )} \\
&\lesssim r^{1/2}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa}+{\vvvert \bar \mathbb{A} \vvvert}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)},
\end{align*}
from Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition}. The Wick powers of $\phi$ only contribute a small power of $(1+\|B\|_{H^1})$. Indeed, tracking the constants behind the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:wick-powers} yields
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[\|\llbracket \phi^i(\phi^*)^j \rrbracket_N\|_{W^{\-eps,q}}^r\big]^{1/r} \lesssim r^{\frac{i+j}{2}}(1+\|B\|_{H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}.
\]
Combining all the factors produces a $\|B\|_{H^1}$ dependence with an acceptable exponent, and this completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:bV_well_defined}
    The renormalised vacuum polarisation $\mathbb{V}_{A_T}$ is integrable, i.e., $\mathbb{V}_{A_T}\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^+;\mathbb{R})$, almost surely for all $T\ge 0$. It therefore holds that $Q_{N,T}(A_T+B_T) = \mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}_T,B_T)$ and the limit
    \[
    \mathcal{Q}_\infty(\mathbf{A}_T,0) = \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}_T,0)
    \]
    is well-defined.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
For a fixed $T$, Lemma \ref{lem:vac_pol_bound} gives the inequality
    \begin{align*}
        |\mathbb{V}_{A_T}(\lambda)| &\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-2}|\vartheta|^2 +(1+\lambda)^{-2} \sum_{|p|^2\le 1+\lambda} (1+|p|^2)|\hat A_T^0(p)|^2 \\
        &+ (1+\lambda)^{-1}\sum_{|p|^2> 1+\lambda} \frac{|p|^2}{|p|^2}|\hat A_T^0(p)|^2 \le (1+\lambda)^{-2} \Big(|\vartheta|^2+\sum_{|p|\le T} \langle p\rangle^2|\hat A_T^0(p)|^2\Big),
    \end{align*}
    which yields an integrable bound up to an a.s. finite constant. The same computation verifies that $\mathbb{E}^\Theta\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[\mathbb{V}_{A_T}]$ is integrable. The remaining claims now follow from our definitions and Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_cQ_N} by dominated convergence.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:bV_properties}
    The sequence $(\mathbb{V}_{A_T})_{T\ge 0}$ converges in $L^2(\bar\,\mathrm{d}\vartheta\otimes\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}};L^1(\mathbb{R}^+;\mathbb{R}))$ to a random limit denoted by $\mathbb{V}_A$. Furthermore, it holds that
    \[
    \int_0^\infty\; \sup_T\mathbb{E}^\Theta\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[|\mathbb{V}_{A_T}(\lambda)|^2]^{1/2}\,\mathrm{d} \lambda <\infty,
    \]
    and $\mathbb{E}^\Theta\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[\|\mathbb{V}_A\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^+;\mathbb{R})}^p]<\infty$ for all $p\ge 1$
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Since $\vartheta$ is bounded and constant in $T$, it is enough to consider the Gaussian part $A_T^0$ and show that $(\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0})_{T\ge 0}$ is Cauchy in the stronger $L^1(\mathbb{R}^+;L^2(\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}}))$ norm, which will imply the first claim. To simplify the computation, we introduce the shorthand notation
    \[
    \hat{A^0}_{T,j,k}(p) \coloneqq \hat{A^0}_{T,j}(p)^* \hat{A^0}_{T,k}(p) \, \textup{ and } \, e_{T,j,k}(p) \coloneqq \frac{(-1)^{j+k}\chi_T(p)^2p_{j+1}p_{k+1}}{|p|^2}.
    \]
    Given any $S,T\ge 0$, we begin by evaluating the expectation
    \begin{align*}
        &\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[\big(\hat{A^0}_{T,j,k}(p)-e_{T,j,k}(p) - (\hat{A^0}_{S,j,k}(p)-e_{S,j,k}(p))\big)^* \times \\
        &\quad\quad \big(\hat{A^0}_{T,j',k'}(p')-e_{T,j',k'}(p') - (\hat{A^0}_{S,j',k'}(p')-e_{S,j',k'}(p'))\big)\big] \\
        &\quad = \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[\hat{A^0}_{T,j,k}(p) \hat{A^0}_{T,j',k'}(p') \big] - \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[\hat{A^0}_{T,j,k}(p) \hat{A^0}_{S,j',k'}(p') \big]  \\
        &\quad\quad - \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[\hat{A^0}_{S,j,k}(p) \hat{A^0}_{T,j',k'}(p') \big] + \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[\hat{A^0}_{S,j,k}(p) \hat{A^0}_{S,j',k'}(p') \big] \\
        &\quad\quad - e_{T,j,k}(p)e_{T,j',k'}(p')  + e_{T,j,k}(p)e_{S,j',k'}(p') + e_{S,j,k}(p)e_{T,j',k'}(p') - e_{S,j,k}(p)e_{S,j',k'}(p') \\
        &\quad = 2e_{T,j,k}(p)e_{T,j',k'}(p) - 2e_{T,j,k}(p)e_{S,j',k'}(p) - 2e_{S,j,k}(p)e_{T,j',k'}(p) + 2e_{S,j,k}(p)e_{S,j',k'}(p)
    \end{align*}
    using Wick's theorem in combination with the covariance of $A_T^0$. This yields the expression
    \begin{align} \label{eq:vac_pol_variance}
        \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[|\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0}(\lambda)-\mathbb{V}_{A_S^0}(\lambda)|^2] = 2\sum_{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2}\sum_{\substack{j,j', \\ k,k'=1}}^2  & \frac{(-1)^{j+j'+k+k'}p_{j+1}p_{k+1}p_{j'+1}p_{k'+1}}{|p|^8}\times \nonumber\\
        &\Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(p)\Pi^\lambda_{j',k'}(p) \big(\chi_T(p)^2-\chi_S(p)^2\big)^2
    \end{align}
    for the variance of the vacuum polarisation. From Lemma \ref{lem:vac_pol_bound}, we obtain the estimates
    \begin{align*}
    |\Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(p)\Pi^\lambda_{j',k'}(p)|\,|p|^{-4}  &\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-9/4}\,|p|^{-7/2} \, \textup{ if } \, |p| > \sqrt{1+\lambda}, \, \textup{ and } \\
    |\Pi^\lambda_{j,k}(p)\Pi^\lambda_{j',k'}(p)|\,|p|^{-4}  &\lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-4} \, \textup{ if } \, |p| \le \sqrt{1+\lambda}.
    \end{align*}
    Without loss of generality we now assume $S\le T$. The above then implies the inequality
    \[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[|\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0}(\lambda)-\mathbb{V}_{A_S^0}(\lambda)|^2] \lesssim (1+\lambda)^{-5/4}\sum_{\substack{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2 \\ |p|^2 \ge 1+\lambda\vee S^2}}  |p|^{-7/2}  + (1+\lambda)^{-4}\sum_{\substack{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2 \\ S^2\le |p|^2 \le 1+\lambda}} 1.
    \]
    We have thus shown that
    \begin{align*}
    ||\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0}-\mathbb{V}_{A_S^0}||_{L^1(\lambda)L^2(\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}})} &\lesssim \Big(\sum_{\substack{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2 \\ |p|^2 \ge S^2}} |p|^{-7/2}\Big)^{1/2}\int_0^\infty\; (1+\lambda)^{-9/8}\,\mathrm{d} \lambda \\
    &\quad\quad\quad\quad + \int_{S^2-1}^\infty\; (1+\lambda)^{-2}\Big(\sum_{\substack{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2 \\ |p|^2 \le 1+\lambda}} 1\Big)^{1/2} \,\mathrm{d} \lambda \\
    &\lesssim \Big(\sum_{\substack{p\in 2\pi{\mathbb Z}^2 \\ |p|^2 \ge S^2}} |p|^{-7/2}\Big)^{1/2} + \int_{S^2-1}^\infty\; (1+\lambda)^{-3/2} \,\mathrm{d} \lambda \xrightarrow{S\to\infty} 0,
    \end{align*}
    as desired. A similar reasoning starting from \eqref{eq:vac_pol_variance} with $S=T-1$ yields the bound
    \[
    ||\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0}-\mathbb{V}_{A_{T-1}^0}||_{L^1(\lambda)L^2(\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}})} \lesssim \frac{1}{(T-1)^{5/4}},
    \]
    which is summable and thus implies an integrable bound for $\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[|\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0}|^2]^{1/2}$ that is uniform in the cut off $T$. We therefore deduce the second claim. We now conclude by noting that $\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0} \xrightarrow{L^2(\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}})} \mathbb{V}_{A^0}$ is a renormalised quadratic functional and hence an element of the second Wiener chaos. It follows from Gaussian hypercontractivity that its higher moments are controlled by the second moment.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
    There exists a $\bar \kappa>0$ such that the following hold for all $\kappa\in (0,\bar \kappa)$. The limit (in any order of $T$ and $N$)
    \[
    \mathcal{Z}(h) \coloneqq \lim_{N,T\to\infty} \mathcal{Z}_{N,T}(h,1)
    \]
    exists for every $h\in C_{{\rm test}}$ for all sufficiently small $c>0$, and satisfies $0 < \mathcal{Z}(h) < \infty$.
    In particular, $\mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}_{N,T}$ converges weakly to a probability measure on $\Omega^1 \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{T}^2)\times \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{T}^2)$.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:cH_identities}
    With $\mathbf{A}_T^0=(A_T^0,A_T^{0\,*} A_T^0-{\mathrm{c}}_T,\mathbb{V}_{A_T^0})$ and $B_T\in\Omega_C^1 H^1$, the identities
    \begin{align*}
    \mathcal{H}^F_{N,T}(A_T^0,\vartheta) &= \mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}_T,0)+\mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}}(\mathbb{A}_T,0), \textup{ and } \\
    \mathcal{H}^F_{N,T}(A_T^0+B_T,\vartheta) &= \mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T})+\mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m_{\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}}}(\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T})
    \end{align*}
    hold $\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}}\times \bar \,\mathrm{d}\vartheta$-almost surely.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
This essentially follows by definition from the properties of the translation operation $\mathbf{A}_T\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B_T$ as defined in~\eqref{eq:translation_bfA}. For the ratio of determinants, the relevant inclusion in the enhanced state space $\mathcal{X}_V^{-\kappa}$ is Corollary~\ref{cor:bV_well_defined}, and then Proposition~\ref{prop:translation_determinant} supplies the desired identity.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:BD_A_bounds}
    Fix $q\ge 1$ and $\varepsilon>0$. For all $T,N\ge 0$, all test functions $h\in C_{{\rm test}}$ with sufficiently small growth parameter $c$, and all drifts $v\in \mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}$, there exist positive, measurable functions $\mathscr{Q}_T$ independent of $v$ (and $N$) and a $C_E>0$ such that
    \begin{align*}
    q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0+B_T,\vartheta) &\ge -\mathscr{Q}_T - (4qC_Ec+\varepsilon) \|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2,\\
    q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta) &\le \mathscr{Q}_T,\\
    \sup_T \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[\mathscr{Q}_T] &\le C(h,\kappa,q,\varepsilon),
    \end{align*}
    with the first two bounds uniform in $N$.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
We rely on the representation of $\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:cH_identities} and consider separately each term that appears there. Note that $\mathrm{d}^*({}_\vartheta{B_T})=0$: the drift $B_T=J_T(v)$ is co-exact by construction and $\vartheta$ is a constant form. Provided that $c$ is small enough, Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs-W-bound} ensures the existence of exponents $\tau(\kappa)$ and ${\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)$ such that, for all $\delta>0$, the inequality
    \begin{align*}
    \mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m_{\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}}}(\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}) &\ge -C(h,\kappa,\delta,\vartheta)\big(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A}_T^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)} + m_{\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}}^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}\big) - \delta\|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)} \\
    &\quad\quad -c \|A_T+{}_\vartheta{B_T}\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2,
    \end{align*}
    holds uniformly in $N$ for some constant $C(h,\kappa,\delta,\vartheta)>0$ and all $\kappa$ small enough. We use here that $\|{}_\vartheta{B_T}\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)} \le 2|\vartheta| +  2\|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)}$ for $\tau(\kappa)\le 1$. For the mass $m_{\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}}$, Lemma~\ref{lem:difference_masses} implies the bound
    \begin{align*}
    m_{\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}} &\le 1 + C(\kappa)(1+\|{}_\vartheta{B_T}\|_{\Omega^1 H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A}_T^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^3),\\
    \shortintertext{which in turn yields}
    C(h,\kappa,\delta,\vartheta) m_{\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}}^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)} &\le C(h,\kappa,\delta,\vartheta) + C(h,\kappa,\delta,\vartheta)(1+\|{}_\vartheta{B_T}\|_{\Omega^1 H^1})^{\tau(\kappa)}(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A}_T^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^3)^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)} \\
    &\le C(h,\kappa,\delta,\vartheta)(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A}_T^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}) + \delta\|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)}
    \end{align*}
    for a suitably redefined $C(h,\kappa,\delta,\vartheta)>0$. By Besov-H\"older embedding, there is an analytic constant $C_E$ (bounded above, for example, by the constant in Bernstein's inequality on $\mathbb{T}^2$) such that
    \[
    c \|A_T+{}_\vartheta{B_T}\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2 \le 2c\|A_T\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2 + 2^{2+\kappa} c |\vartheta| + 4c C_E \|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^2.
    \]
    Combining the above, we obtain
    \[
    q\mathcal{W}_N^{h,q,m_{\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}}}(\mathbb{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}) \ge -C(h,\kappa,\delta,q,\vartheta)\big(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A}^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}\big) - 2q\delta\|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^{\tau(\kappa)} - 4qc C_E \|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^2
    \]
    valid for all $\kappa$ small enough. Arguing similarly starting from the upper bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs-W-bound}, we also see that
    \[
    q\mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}}(\mathbb{A}_T,0) \le C(h,\kappa,\delta,q,\vartheta)\big(1+{\vvvert \mathbb{A}^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)}\big)
    \]
    for a possibly larger $C(h,\kappa,\delta,q,\vartheta)>0$. For the ratio of determinants, Theorems~\ref{thm:lower_bound_det} and~\ref{thm:convergence_cQ_N} give the lower and upper bounds, respectively,
    \begin{align*}
    q\mathcal{Q}_{N}(\mathbf{A}_T^0,{}_\vartheta{B_T}) &\ge -C(\kappa,\delta,q,\vartheta)(1+{\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}_T^0\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)} - q\delta\|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}^{1+\tau(\kappa)},\\
    q\mathcal{Q}_{N}(\mathbf{A}_T) &\le C(\kappa,q,\vartheta)(1+{\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}_T^0\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa})^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)},
    \end{align*}
    both uniformly in $N$. Choosing $\delta\le \varepsilon/(3q)$ and noting that $\|B_T\|_{\Omega^1 H^1}\le \|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}$, we thus arrive at the desired inequalities for $q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(\cdot,\vartheta)$ with
    \[
    \mathscr{Q}_T = C(h,\kappa,\varepsilon,q,\vartheta)(1+{\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}_T^0\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa}^{{\mathrm{n}}(\kappa)})
    \]
    independent of $v$ and $N$. As $\vartheta$ varies over a compact set, we may drop the $\vartheta$-dependence by replacing the constant above by its supremum over $\vartheta\in {\mathbf i} (0,2\pi]^2$. The uniform bound on $\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[\mathscr{Q}_T]$ now follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:bV_properties} and the standard two-dimensional estimate
    \[
    \sup_T \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[{\vvvert \mathbb{A}_T^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^N]<\infty, \textup{ for all } \kappa>0,N\in\mathbb{N}.
    \]
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:tameness_lower_bound}
    For all test functions $h\in C_{{\rm test}}$ with sufficiently small $c>0$, and all $N,T\ge 0$, the functional $q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)$ is bounded from below by
    \[
    q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta) \ge - C(q,T,N,h) -2qc \|A_T^0\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2
    \]
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
It suffices to consider the case $q=1$. Note that $m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0} \le 1+{\mathrm{c}}_T<\infty$ for any finite $T$. Moreover, by assumption, we have
    \begin{align*}
    |h(A_T,\phi_{\mathbb{A}_T,0,N})| &\le c+c \|A_T\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2 + c \|\phi_{\mathbb{A}_T,0,N}\|_{H^{-\kappa}}^{2n} \\
    &\le C(h,\vartheta)+c\|\phi_{\mathbb{A}_T,0,N}\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n} + 2c \|A_T^0\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2
    \end{align*}
    for any $T$ and $N$. We may drop the $\vartheta$ dependence as before by compactness. For any $c<c_n$, the lead coefficient of the Higgs interaction potential, we thus see that
    \begin{align*}
    -|h(A_T,\phi_{\mathbb{A}_T,0,N})|+{\mathscr{V}}_N^{m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}}(\phi_{\mathbb{A}_T,0,N}) &\ge -C(N,T,h) - 2c \|A_T^0\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2,\\
    \shortintertext{and hence}
    \mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}}(\mathbb{A}_T,0) &\ge -C(T,N,h) - 2c \|A_T^0\|_{\Omega^1 C^{-\kappa/2}}^2.
    \end{align*}
    We consider the difference of resolvents in $Q_{N,T}$ next. It suffices to study the trace for $\lambda=0$. With a view to using the heat kernel representation in Lemma \ref{lem:semi-group}, we note that the diamagnetic inequality implies that
    \[
    0\le p_{\mathbb{A}_T}(t,x,x) \le p_0(t,0)
    \]
    on the diagonal, and so, by definition of $m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}$,
    \[
    e^{-t}p_0(t,0)-e^{-(m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}-{\mathrm{c}}_T)t}p_{\mathbb{A}_T}(t,x,x) \ge (1-e^{{\mathrm{c}}_T t})p_0(t,0).
    \]
    Since the spectrum of $L_{\mathbb{A}_T}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}$ is bounded below by $1$, the semi-group property of the covariant heat kernel yields the estimate (for $t\ge 1$):
    \[
    e^{-(m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}-{\mathrm{c}}_T)t}p_{\mathbb{A}_T}(t,x,x) \le e^{-(t-1)}e^{-(m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}-{\mathrm{c}}_T)}p_{\mathbb{A}_T}(1,x,x) \le e^{1+{\mathrm{c}}_T -t}p_1(0).
    \]
    We now see that
    \begin{align*}
    \int_0^\infty\; e^{-t}p_0(t,0) -  e^{-(m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}-{\mathrm{c}}_T)t}p_{\mathbb{A}_T}(t,x,x)\,\mathrm{d} t &\ge \int_0^1\; (1-e^{{\mathrm{c}}_T t})p_0(t,0)\,\mathrm{d} t \\
    &\quad\quad + \int_1^\infty\; e^{-t}p_0(t,0) - e^{1-t}e^{{\mathrm{c}}_T}p_1(0)\,\mathrm{d} t,
    \end{align*}
    which is bounded below depending on ${\mathrm{c}}_T$. It follows that
    \[
    \int_0^N \operatorname{Tr} \Big((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1}-(L_{\mathbb{A}_T}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}+\lambda)^{-1} \Big)\,\mathrm{d} \lambda \ge -C(N,T).
    \]
   Finally, the remaining terms in $Q_{N,T}$ are likewise bounded (from above and below) by a constant depending on $T$ and $N$.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:tameness_A}
    Fix $q\ge 1$. For all test functions $h\in C_{{\rm test}}$ with sufficiently small $c>0$, the functional $q \mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)$ is tame with respect to $\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}}$, that is, it satisfies
    \[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[|q \mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)|^{r_1}] + \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[e^{-r_2 q \mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)}] < \infty
    \]
    for some $r_1,r_2\ge 1$ such that $\frac{1}{r_1}+\frac{1}{r_2}=1$.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
For the exponential bound, it is enough to consider the quadratic norm stemming from the test function $h$ thanks to Lemma \ref{lem:tameness_lower_bound}. But $\exp(\alpha {\vvvert \mathbb{A}_T^0 \vvvert}_{-\kappa}^2)$ is integrable for all sufficiently small $\alpha>0$ by Fernique's theorem, and hence \[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[e^{-r_2 q \mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)}] < \infty,
    \]
    for a suitably restricted $c$ (essentially depending only on $q$ and analytic constants, as we may choose $r_2$ arbitrarily close to one). For the $L^2(\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}})$ bound, we rely on the estimate from Lemma~\ref{lem:BD_A_bounds}, the existence of all moments for Gaussians and Lemma~\ref{lem:bV_properties} in relation to the vacuum polarisation.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:unif_integrability}
    Given a fixed $q\ge 1$, there exists a $\tilde c(q)>0$ such that, for any $h\in C_{{\rm test}}$ with $c<\tilde c$, we have the uniform bounds
    \[
    0 < \inf_{N,T} \mathcal{Z}_{N,T}(h,q) \le \sup_{N,T} \mathcal{Z}_{N,T}(h,q) < \infty.
    \]
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
We disintegrate the partition function as follows:
    \[
    \mathcal{Z}_{N,T}(h,q) = \int_{{\mathbf i} (0,2\pi]^2}\;\exp\Big((-)- \log\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[e^{-q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)} \big]\Big)\,\bar \mathrm{d}\vartheta.
    \]
    First, choose $c$ small enough for Lemma~\ref{lem:BD_A_bounds} and Corollary~\ref{cor:tameness_A} to hold. We thereby obtain the representation
    \[
    -\log \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[e^{-q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)}]=\inf_{v\in\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\Big[q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0+J_T(v),\vartheta)+ \frac 1 2\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2\Big]
    \]
    for the expression inside the exponential above from the Bou\'e-Dupuis formula. Lemma \ref{lem:BD_A_bounds}, for any $\varepsilon>0$, implies the lower bound
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\Big[q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0+J_T(v),\vartheta) &+ \frac 1 2\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2\Big] \ge -\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[\mathscr{Q}_T\big] + (\tfrac 1 2-4qC_E c-\varepsilon)\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\big[\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2\big].
    \end{align*}
    We now impose the further requirement $c < (8q C_E)^{-1}$ (which, together with the previous constraints, defines $\tilde c(q)$) and choose $\varepsilon< \tfrac 1 2-4qC_Ec$ to infer that
    \[
    \inf_{v\in\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\Big[q\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0+J_T(v),\vartheta) + \frac 1 2\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2\Big] \ge -C(h,q,\varepsilon),
    \]
    uniformly in $T$ and $N$. Taking $v=0$ in the upper bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:BD_A_bounds} gives a uniform upper bound for the variational functional. Since both bounds are uniform in $\vartheta$, they remain valid after the final expectation over $\vartheta$, completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:A_convergence}
    \begin{enumerate}
        \par\hangindent 40\p@   For a fixed $T\in [0,\infty]$, the limit
                \[
                \mathcal{H}_{\infty,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta) \coloneqq \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)
                \]
                exists $\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}}$-almost surely.\\
        \par\hangindent 40\p@   For a fixed $N\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$, the random variables
                \[
                \mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)
                \]
                converge in probability as $T\to\infty$ on $(\Omega^{\mathrm{A}},\mathcal F^{\mathrm{A}},\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}})$, uniformly in $N$ and $\vartheta$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Assume first that $T$ and $N$ are finite. The existence of the $N\to\infty$ limit of $Q_{N,T}(A_T)=\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}_T)$ follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_cQ_N} via Corollary~\ref{cor:bV_well_defined}. The limit of $\mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}}(\mathbb{A}_T,0)$ is a direct consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs_convergence}.

    For the second claim, Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs_convergence} states that $\mathcal{W}_N^{h,1,m_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}}(\mathbb{A}_T,0)$ is a locally Lipschitz continuous function of $\mathbb{A}_T^0$ in the ${\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\cdot;\cdot\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa}$ topology, uniformly in $N$. Lemma~\ref{lem:Rem_det} implies that $\mathbf{A}_T^0\mapsto\mathcal{Q}_N(\mathbf{A}_T)$ is also continuous in the ${\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\cdot;\cdot\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa}$ topology, again uniformly in $N$. Lemma~\ref{lem:bV_properties} confirms that $\mathbf{A}_T^0$ converges in probability as $T\to\infty$, and $\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)$ thus also converges in probability. Since ${\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}_T-\bar\mathbf{A}_T\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa} \lesssim {\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}_T^0-\bar\mathbf{A}_T^0\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa}$, the convergence is uniform also in $\vartheta$.

    To conclude, observe that we have actually shown that $\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)$, as a random variable in $(\Omega^{\mathrm{A}},\mathcal h^{\mathrm{A}},\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}})$, is an equicontinuous (in $N$ and $\vartheta$) function of $\mathbf{A}_T^0$. The pointwise limit of that function as $N\to\infty$ thus also implies the convergence (in probability) of $\mathcal{H}_{\infty,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)$. By the same pointwise convergence, that limit must be the same as the limit obtained by first taking $T\to\infty$, followed by $N\to\infty$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:continuity}
    Let the assumptions of Proposition \ref{prop:unif_integrability} hold, and let $\mathbb{A}_T^0$ and $\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)$ be as defined in Section~\ref{sec:gauge_variational_setup}. As $T\to\infty$, the sequence of random variables
    \[
    e^{-\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)}
    \]
    converges in distribution on the probability space $({\mathbf i} (0,2\pi]^2,\bar\mathrm{d}\vartheta)\times(\Omega^{\mathrm{A}},\mathcal h^{\mathrm{A}},\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm{A}})$ for any $N\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Since the random zero mode $\vartheta$ is constant in $T$, the proposition is a direct consequence of Lemma~\ref{lem:A_convergence} and the continuity of the (real) exponential function.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Choose $q>1$ arbitrarily close to one, fixing the admissible class $C_{{\rm test}}$ with the range $c \in (0,\tilde c(q))$ depending on $q$ through Proposition~\ref{prop:unif_integrability}. For any test function in this class, Proposition~\ref{prop:unif_integrability} gives uniform integrability of the family $e^{-\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)}$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:continuity}, this family converges in law as $T\to\infty$ for any $N\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$, uniformly in $N$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:A_convergence}. The expectations therefore converge uniformly in $N$:
    \[
    \lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb{E}^\Theta\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\Big[e^{-\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)}\Big] = \mathbb{E}^\Theta\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\Big[\lim_{T\to\infty} e^{-\mathcal{H}_{N,T}^h(A_T^0,\vartheta)}\Big].
    \]
    The bounds $0<\mathcal{Z}(h)<\infty$ are a direct consequence of Proposition~\ref{prop:unif_integrability}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:gauge_invariance_Q_V}
    We have for smooth $A$ and $g$
    \[
    \mathcal{Q}_{N,T}(A^{g})=\mathcal{Q}_{N,T}(A), \qquad \mathcal{V}_{A^{g},N,T}({\boldsymbol{\cdot}})=\mathcal{V}_{A,N,T}({\boldsymbol{\cdot}}).
    \]
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
The statement regarding $\mathcal{V}$ is trivial as the dependence in $A$ is through $\lambda_{A,N,T}$ which is gauge-invariant for being defined through the spectrum of the operator $L_{A}$ and $L_{A^g}=gL_Ag^{-1}$.

    Regarding $\mathcal{Q}$, we first treat the integral in its definition. We write
\begin{align*}
\int_0^T &\operatorname{Tr} \Big((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1}-(L_{A^g}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+\lambda_{A^g,T}+\lambda)^{-1}) \Big)\,\mathrm{d} \lambda \\
&=
\int_0^T \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0^+}\operatorname{Tr} \Big((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon}-(L_{A^g}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+\lambda_{A^g,T}+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon}) \Big)\,\mathrm{d} \lambda \\
&=
\int_0^T \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0^+}\left\{\operatorname{Tr} \big((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon}\big)-\operatorname{Tr}\big(g(L_{A}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+\lambda_{A,T}+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon} g^{-1}\big)\right\}\,\mathrm{d} \lambda \\
&=
\int_0^T \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0^+}\left\{\operatorname{Tr} \big((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon}\big)-\operatorname{Tr}\big((L_{A}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+\lambda_{A,T}+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon} \big)\right\}\,\mathrm{d} \lambda \\
&=
\int_0^T \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0^+}\operatorname{Tr} \Big((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon}-(L_{A}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+\lambda_{A,T}+\lambda)^{-1-\varepsilon} \Big)\,\mathrm{d} \lambda,
\end{align*}
where the first equality is by dominated convergence, the second one by $L_{A^g}=gL_Ag^{-1}$, the third one by cyclicity, and the last one by linearity.
Afterwards, we apply dominated convergence to get the gauge-invariance of the integral.
Moreover, the other term in $\mathcal{Q}_{N,T}$ is defined through $\lambda_{A,N,T}$ which is also gauge-invariant and therefore proving that $\mathcal{Q}_{N,T}$ is gauge-invariant.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
We have by the definition of $\mu^{{\mathrm{A}}[g]}_T$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:gauge_invariance_Q_V}
\begin{align*}
\int F(A,\phi) \,\mathrm{d}\mu_{N,T}^{{\mathrm{YMH}}[g]}(A,\phi)&=\frac{1}{\mathcal{Z}_{N,T}^{[g]}}\int F(A^{g_T},\phi)
    e^{-\mathcal{Q}_{N,T}(A^{g_T})-\mathcal{V}_{A^{g_T},N,T}(\phi)}
    \,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{GFF}}}_{A^{g_T},N,T}(\phi)\,\mathrm{d}\mu_T^{{\mathrm{A}}}(A)\\
    &=\frac{1}{\mathcal{Z}_{N,T}^{[g]}}\int F(A^{g_T},\phi)
    e^{-\mathcal{Q}_{N,T}(A)-\mathcal{V}_{A,N,T}(\phi)}
    \,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{GFF}}}_{A^{g_T},N,T}(\phi)\,\mathrm{d}\mu_T^{{\mathrm{A}}}(A).
\end{align*}
Furthermore, recalling~\ref{eq:intro_covariant_GFF},  $\mu^{{\mathrm{GFF}}}_{A^{g_T},N,T}$ is the law of
    \begin{equation*}
    \phi_{A^{g_T},N,T}
    =\int_0^N
    \bigl(L_{A^{g_T}}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+\lambda_{A^{g_T},T}+\lambda\bigr)^{-1}
    \,\mathrm{d} X^{\Phi}_\lambda,
\end{equation*}
and $\lambda_{A,T}$ is gauge-invariant can be written as
    \begin{equation*}
    \phi_{A^{g_T},N,T}
    =g_T\int_0^N
    \bigl(L_{A}-{\mathrm{c}}_T+\lambda_{A,T}+\lambda\bigr)^{-1}
    g_T^{-1}\,\mathrm{d} X^{\Phi}_\lambda.
\end{equation*}
Since $g_T^{-1}$ is unitary we have that $g_T^{-1} X_\Lambda^\Phi$ has the same law as $X_\lambda^\Phi$ and as such $\mu^{{\mathrm{GFF}}}_{A^{g_T},N,T}$ is the law of  $g_T\phi_{A,N,T}$.

This allow us to write
\begin{align*}
\int F(A,\phi) \,\mathrm{d}\mu_{N,T}^{{\mathrm{YMH}}[g]}(A,\phi)&=\frac{1}{\mathcal{Z}_{N,T}^{[g]}}\int F(A^{g_T},g_T\phi)
    e^{-\mathcal{Q}_{N,T}(A)-\mathcal{V}_{A,N,T}(g_T\phi)}
    \,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{GFF}}}_{A,N,T}(\phi)\,\mathrm{d}\mu_T^{{\mathrm{A}}}(A)\\
  &=  \frac{1}{\mathcal{Z}_{N,T}^{[g]}}\int F(A^{g_T},g_T\phi)
    e^{-\mathcal{Q}_{N,T}(A)-\mathcal{V}_{A,N,T}(\phi)}
    \,\mathrm{d}\mu^{{\mathrm{GFF}}}_{A,N,T}(\phi)\,\mathrm{d}\mu_T^{{\mathrm{A}}}(A),
\end{align*}
where we have used that $\mathcal{V}_{A,N,T}(g_T\phi)=\mathcal{V}_{A,N,T}(\phi)$ due to the fact that it is a polynomial in $|\phi|$ and $g_T$ is unitary.  Hence,
\begin{align}\label{eq:gauge_covariance_cutoff}
\int F(A,\phi) \,\mathrm{d}\mu_{N,T}^{{\mathrm{YMH}}[g]}(A,\phi)&=\int F(A^{g_T},g_T\phi) \,\mathrm{d}\mu_{N,T}^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi),
\end{align}
and taking limits yields the result.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
By the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:gauge_covariance}, we have found
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:linear_covariant_gauges_cutoff}
\int F(A,\phi)\,\mathrm{d} \mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}(\alpha)}_{N,T}(A,\phi)=\int F(A^{{\mathscr g}_T^{\alpha^{-1/2}\zeta}},{\mathscr g}_T^{\alpha^{-1/2}\zeta}\phi)\,\mathrm{d} \mu^{{\mathrm{YMH}}}_{N,T}(A,\phi)  \,\mathrm{d}\nu(\zeta),
\end{equation}
so that taking limits yields the desired statement. Finally, the limit $\alpha\to \infty$ follows from the fact that $g^{\alpha^{-1/2}\zeta}\to 1$ in $C^{1-\delta}$ for any $\delta>0$ and hereby we obtain the result for $\alpha\to\infty$.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:deterministic_variational_problem}
For every $\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2$, one has
\begin{align*}
\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)
&:=\inf_{\substack{v\in\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}_0\\u\in\mathbb{H}^\Phi_0}}
\Big\{
  \mathcal{G}^{f;0}\bigl(\0\mathbin{\pmb{+}}(\vartheta+J(v)),u\bigr)
  +\frac12\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2
\Big\}\\
&=\inf_{\substack{A\in\mathcal A_\vartheta\\\phi\in H^1}}
\Big\{
  f(A,\phi)+\mathcal{S}_{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi)
\Big\}.
\end{align*}
Moreover, if $f$ is bounded and Lipschitz, then $\vartheta\mapsto\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)$ is bounded and continuous on ${\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2$.
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
We rewrite the infimum over controls as an infimum over the fields $A=\vartheta+J(v)$ and $\phi=I^{\0\mathbin{\pmb{+}} A}(u)$. For fixed $(A,\phi)\in\mathcal A_\vartheta\times H^1$, the observable and potential are fixed, so we only need to minimize the control energy. Set $\mathbb{A}=\0\mathbin{\pmb{+}} A$. Then $L_{\mathbb{A},0}=L_A$ and $m_{\mathbb{A},0}=1$, and the minimum control energy is
\[
\inf_{\substack{J(v)=A-\vartheta\\I^\mathbb{A}(u)=\phi}}
\frac12\bigl(\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2+\|u\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}^2\bigr)
=\frac12\bigl(\|\mathrm{d} A\|_{L^2}^2+\|\mathrm{d}_A\phi\|_{L^2}^2+\|\phi\|_{L^2}^2\bigr).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives the lower bound. The Hodge decomposition and spectral calculus show that it is attained by
\[
v_t^*=\mathbf1_{[0,1]}(t)\,\mathrm{d} A,
\qquad
u_t^*=(L_A+1)(L_A+1+t)^{-1}\phi.
\]
The term $-\frac12\|\phi\|_{L^2}^2$ in $\mathcal{V}_\mathbb{A}^0(\phi)$ cancels the last term above, so the minimum cost at fixed $(A,\phi)$ is $f(A,\phi)+\mathcal{S}_{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi)$. Every pair in $\mathcal A_\vartheta\times H^1$ is produced by these controls, so taking the infimum over the pairs proves the identity.

Since $f$ is bounded and $\mathcal V$ is bounded below, comparison with $(A,\phi)=(\vartheta,0)$ gives
\[
-C\leq\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)
\leq f(\vartheta,0)+|\mathbb{T}^2|\mathcal V(0)
\leq C,
\]
with $C$ independent of $\vartheta$.

For continuity, fix $0<\eta\leq1$ and choose $(A,\phi)\in\mathcal A_\vartheta\times H^1$ such that
\[
f(A,\phi)+\mathcal{S}_{{\mathrm{YMH}}}(A,\phi)
\leq\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)+\eta.
\]
Since $\mathcal V(r)\ge r-C$ for $r\ge0$, the preceding upper bound and boundedness of $f$ give $\|\mathrm{d}_A\phi\|_{L^2}^2+\|\phi\|_{L^2}^2\leq C$, independently of $\vartheta$ and $\eta$. Set $h=\vartheta'-\vartheta$. The pair $(A+h,\phi)$ belongs to $\mathcal A_{\vartheta'}\times H^1$, and $\mathrm{d}_{A+h}\phi=\mathrm{d}_A\phi+h\phi$. Comparing the two costs and using that $f$ is Lipschitz gives
\[
\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta')
\leq\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)+\eta+C(|h|+|h|^2).
\]
Letting $\eta\downarrow0$ and interchanging $\vartheta$ and $\vartheta'$ proves continuity.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:easy_theorem}
Let $f$ be a bounded Lipschitz observable. Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2$,
\[
\mathcal F^{f;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)
\leq \mathcal F_0^{f;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\sup_{\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2}
\Big(
\mathcal F_0^{f;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)
-\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)
\Big)
\leq 0.
\]
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
The first inequality follows by restricting both infima to deterministic controls.

For the second inequality, we first note that the pair $\mathbb{A}=\0\mathbin{\pmb{+}}(\vartheta+J(v))$ has $m_{\mathbb{A},0}=1$. Since $f$ is bounded and $r\mapsto\mathcal V(r)-r/2$ is bounded below on $[0,\infty)$, the expression minimized in $\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)$ is at least $\frac12(\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2+\|u\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}^2)-C$, uniformly in $\vartheta$. Testing with zero controls gives a uniform upper bound, so the infimum defining $\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)$ can be restricted to
\[
\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2+\|u\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}^2\leq R
\]
for some $R$ independent of $\vartheta$.

On this set, the resolvent estimate \eqref{eq:pushed_resolvent_difference}, the GFF decomposition of Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:wick-powers} give convergence of the expected controlled Higgs costs to their deterministic limits. Indeed, the shifts and masses converge, while each term of positive noise Wick degree carries a positive power of $\sqrt\varepsilon$. The polynomial bounds in these estimates and the Gaussian moment bounds make the convergence uniform over the bounded controls and $\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2$. The determinant contribution tends to zero uniformly on the same set by Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_cQ_N} and the enhanced gauge-field moment bounds.

Testing $\mathcal F_0^{f;\varepsilon}$ with these bounded controls and taking their infimum therefore gives
\[
\mathcal F_0^{f;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)
\leq\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)+o(1),
\]
uniformly in $\vartheta$, which proves the second inequality.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:lower_bound}
Let $f$ be a bounded Lipschitz observable. Then
\[
\liminf_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\inf_{\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2}
\Bigl(
\mathcal F^{f;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)
-\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)
\Bigr)
\geq0.
\]
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
We compare the stochastic and deterministic costs on events where the control energy is bounded. Coercivity makes large control energies unlikely for controls whose expected cost is close to the infimum, while a moment bound on the negative part of the cost limits how much these rare events can lower the expectation.

Write $\mathbb{E}=\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\mathbb{E}^\Phi$. For fixed $\vartheta$ and controls $v,u$, set
\[
B=\vartheta+J(v),
\qquad
\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon=\mathbb{A}^\varepsilon\mathbin{\pmb{+}} J(v),
\qquad
\mathbb{A}_v^0=\0\mathbin{\pmb{+}} B,
\qquad
U=\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2+\|u\|_{\mathbb{H}^\Phi}^2.
\]
Let $K_\varepsilon(v,u)$ denote the cost before taking expectations, with the determinant left out:
\[
K_\varepsilon(v,u)
:=
f\bigl(A^\varepsilon+J(v),\phi_{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}^\varepsilon+I^{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}(u)\bigr)
+\mathcal{V}_{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}^\varepsilon\bigl(\phi_{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}^\varepsilon+I^{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}(u)\bigr)
+\frac12 U.
\]
Define $K_0$ by the same formula at $\varepsilon=0$, with enhanced pair $\mathbb{A}_v^0$ and Higgs noise zero.

For sufficiently small $\kappa$, there are $p>1$, $\alpha<2$, constants $C,M<\infty$, and nonnegative random variables $R_\varepsilon(v)$, independent of $u$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ld_coercive_estimates}
K_\varepsilon(v,u)\geq\frac14 U-R_\varepsilon(v),
\qquad
\mathbb{E}^\Phi[R_\varepsilon(v)^p]
\leq C\bigl(1+{\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}}\hspace{0.1em}\mathbf{A}^\varepsilon\hspace{0.1em}\raisebox{-3pt}{\rule{2.2pt}{12pt}} \hspace{0.1em}}{}_{-\kappa}\bigr)^M
\bigl(1+\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}\bigr)^\alpha,
\end{equation}
uniformly in $0<\varepsilon\leq1$ and $\vartheta$. To obtain this estimate, repeat the shifted Wick expansion in Lemma~\ref{lem:potential-bound-higgs} with noise $\sqrt\varepsilon\,\phi_{0,B}$. The pure leading term is still $c_n\|Z\|_{L^{2n}}^{2n}$, where $Z=I^{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}(u)+\phi_{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}^\varepsilon-\sqrt\varepsilon\,\phi_{0,B}$. Young's inequality absorbs the lower powers and the mass correction into a fraction of this term. Lemma~\ref{lem:coercive-bound-higgs}, the drift estimate from~\eqref{eq:pushed_resolvent}, and Theorem~\ref{thm:cov_GFF_decomposition} absorb the remaining $\|Z\|_{H_B^s}^{3/2}$ term into the Higgs control energy, with $1-1/n<s<1-4\kappa$. Taking moments of the random remainder, using Lemma~\ref{lem:wick-powers} and the GFF decomposition, gives the conditional moment bound.

Next, choose adapted controls $v^\varepsilon,u^\varepsilon$, with $u^\varepsilon$ chosen measurably in the gauge realization, so that their total expected cost in the iterated variational formula is within $2\varepsilon$ of $\mathcal F^{f;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)$. Theorem~\ref{thm:lower_bound_det}, with $1+\tau(\kappa)<2$, gives, writing $x^-:=\max\{-x,0\}$,
\[
\varepsilon\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\bigl[\mathcal{Q}_\infty(\mathbf{A}^\varepsilon\mathbin{\pmb{+}} J(v),0)^-\bigr]
\leq C\varepsilon\bigl(1+\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\|v\|_{\mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{A}}}^2\bigr).
\]
The estimates in~\eqref{eq:ld_coercive_estimates}, Young's inequality, and the uniform upper bound from Theorem~\ref{thm:easy_theorem} therefore imply, for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$,
\[
\mathbb{E} U(v^\varepsilon,u^\varepsilon)\leq C,
\qquad
\mathbb{E}\bigl[(K_\varepsilon(v^\varepsilon,u^\varepsilon)^-)^p\bigr]\leq C.
\]
For the second bound, use $K_\varepsilon^-\leq R_\varepsilon$ from the first estimate in~\eqref{eq:ld_coercive_estimates} and the conditional moment bound from the second. Young's inequality absorbs the subquadratic power of $\|v^\varepsilon\|$ using its second-moment bound and the gauge-field moment bounds.

For each fixed $R\geq1$, the resolvent difference estimate~\eqref{eq:pushed_resolvent_difference}, Lemma~\ref{lem:difference_masses}, and the same Wick expansion give
\[
\mathbb{E}\Bigl[\mathbf1_{\{U\leq R\}}
\bigl|K_\varepsilon(v,u)-K_0(v,u)\bigr|\Bigr]
\leq r_\varepsilon(R),
\qquad
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}r_\varepsilon(R)=0.
\]
For fixed $R$, the estimates above show that $\|I^{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon}(u)-I^{\mathbb{A}_v^0}(u)\|_{H_B^s}$ and $|m_{\mathbb{A}_v^\varepsilon,0}-1|$ tend to zero in mean as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, after restriction to $\{U\leq R\}$. Here $m_{\mathbb{A}_v^0,0}=1$. Each term of positive noise Wick degree carries a positive power of $\sqrt\varepsilon$. The polynomial bounds, Gaussian moments, and Lipschitz continuity of $f$ make the convergence uniform in $\vartheta$ and in the controls.

Every realization of the controls satisfies $K_0(v,u)\geq\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:deterministic_variational_problem}. Split the expectation according to $U(v^\varepsilon,u^\varepsilon)\leq R$. Markov and H\"older inequalities, the two uniform bounds above, and boundedness of $\mathcal F^{f;0}$ yield
\begin{align*}
\mathcal F^{f;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)+2\varepsilon
&\geq\mathbb{E} K_\varepsilon(v^\varepsilon,u^\varepsilon)-C\varepsilon\\
&\geq\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)
-r_\varepsilon(R)-C R^{-(1-1/p)}-C\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
By taking $R$ large, then $\varepsilon$ small depending on $R$, we obtain the claimed uniform lower bound.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{thm:easy_theorem} and Lemma~\ref{lem:lower_bound}, applied with $f$ and $0$, give
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}
\sup_{\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2}
\bigl|\mathcal F^{g;\varepsilon}(\vartheta)-\mathcal F^{g;0}(\vartheta)\bigr|
=0,
\qquad g\in\{f,0\}.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:deterministic_variational_problem}, the limiting functions are continuous in $\vartheta$.

Laplace principle applied to the integration of $\vartheta$ on ${\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2$, along with the uniform convergence above therefore imply
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\bigl(-\varepsilon\log\mathcal{Z}^\varepsilon(g)\bigr)
=\inf_{\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2}\mathcal F^{g;0}(\vartheta),
\qquad g\in\{f,0\}.
\]
Taking the difference, as in~\eqref{eq:normalized_laplace_functional}, yields
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}D^{f,\varepsilon}
=\inf_{\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2}\mathcal F^{f;0}(\vartheta)
-\inf_{\vartheta\in{\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2}\mathcal F^{0;0}(\vartheta).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:deterministic_variational_problem}, these are the infima of $f+\mathcal{S}_{{\mathrm{YMH}}}$ and $\mathcal{S}_{{\mathrm{YMH}}}$ over Coulomb-gauge fields with harmonic component in ${\mathbf i}[0,2\pi]^2$. Proposition~\ref{prop:coulomb_representative} and gauge invariance identify them with the corresponding infima over $\Omega^1 H^1\times H^1$, proving the theorem.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:norm_comparison_pos_op}
    Let $X$ and $Y$ be positive self-adjoint (unbounded) operators on a Hilbert space $V$ satisfying $\|Xv\|_V\leq C\|Yv\|_V$. Then, for any $s\in[0,1]$,
    \[
    \|X^s v\|_V\leq C^s\|Y^sv\|_V.
    \]
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
The hypothesis gives $X^2\leq C^2Y^2$ in the sense of quadratic forms. Since $t\mapsto t^s$ is operator monotone for $s\in[0,1]$, we obtain
\[
X^{2s}=(X^2)^s\leq(C^2Y^2)^s=C^{2s}Y^{2s}.
\]
Taking quadratic forms yields $\|X^sv\|_V^2\leq C^{2s}\|Y^sv\|_V^2$, and taking square roots proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:interpolation_hilbert_scale}
Let $V$ be a Hilbert space and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $V$ satisfying $A\ge cI$ for some $c>0$. For $s\in\mathbb{R}$, let $V^s$ be the completion of ${\mathscr{D}}(A^{s/2})$ in the norm $\|v\|_{V^s}:=\|A^{s/2}v\|_V$.
If $T$ is linear and bounded $T:V^{s_j}\to V^{t_j}$ for $j=0,1$, then for every
$\theta\in[0,1]$,
\begin{gather*}
T:V^{(1-\theta)s_0+\theta s_1}\to V^{(1-\theta)t_0+\theta t_1}, \\
\|T\|_{V^{(1-\theta)s_0+\theta s_1}\to V^{(1-\theta)t_0+\theta t_1}}
\le
\|T\|_{V^{s_0}\to V^{t_0}}^{1-\theta}\,
\|T\|_{V^{s_1}\to V^{t_1}}^{\theta}.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:ratio_det_Galerkin}
  Let
  \[
    \bar p_M\coloneq2\operatorname{Tr}\int_0^\infty
      P_M(L_0+1+\lambda)^{-2}P_M\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
  \]
  With the deterministic counterterm
  \[
    {\mathrm{o}}_{T,M}\coloneq\frac{{\mathrm{c}}_T}{2}\bar p_M
      -\mathbb{E}^\Theta\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}\left[\int_0^\infty
        \boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda(A_T,A_T)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\right],
  \]
  one has
  \begin{align*}
    e^{-\mathcal{Q}_\infty(\mathbf{A}_T,0)}
    =\lim_{M\rightarrow\infty}
      &\exp\left(\frac{\lambda_{A_T,T}-1}{2}\bar p_M-{\mathrm{o}}_{T,M}\right) \\
      &\times
      \frac{\det_M(P_MH_{A,T}^{-1}P_M)}
           {\det_M(P_M(L_0+1)^{-1}P_M)}\exp\left(\frac{1}{4\pi}\|A_{T}\|^2_{L^2}\right).
  \end{align*}
  Here $\det_M$ denotes the determinant on the complex space
  $\operatorname{range}P_M$.
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
\label{rem:det-counterterm}
    After the mass subtraction, $\exp(-\mathcal{Q}_\infty(\mathbf{A}_T,0))$ matches with the finite dimensional ratio of determinants only up to a constant counterterm, and more importantly a quadratic (but finite) counterterm in $A$. This quadratic counterterm, which is also present in \cite{BC24_YM} is a reflection of the breaking of gauge invariance due to the Galerkin approximation. The cutoff in the main body of the paper is Gauge invariant, as would be true for a lattice cutoff, and there such a counterterm is not present.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Set $B_M\coloneq(P_MH_{A,T}^{-1}P_M)^{-1}$ on $P_ML^2$. The  identity
  \[
    \log a-\log b=\int_0^\infty
      \left(\frac{1}{b+\lambda}-\frac{1}{a+\lambda}\right)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
  \]
  and the spectral theorem give
  \begin{align*}
    \log
      \frac{\det_M(P_MH_{A,T}^{-1}P_M)}
           {\det_M(P_M(L_0+1)^{-1}P_M)}
    =\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(& (B_M+\lambda)^{-1} \\
      &{}-P_M(L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1}P_M\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
  \end{align*}
  We claim that
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:compressed-resolvents}
    \int_0^\infty\left|\operatorname{Tr}\left((B_M+\lambda)^{-1}
      -P_M(H_{A,T}+\lambda)^{-1}P_M\right)\right|\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
      \xrightarrow{M\rightarrow\infty}0.
  \end{equation}

  Assuming the claim, define
  \begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\lambda,M}(A_T,A_T)
    &\coloneq \sum_{p\in 2\pi \mathbb Z^2}\sum_{j,k=1}^2
      \widehat{A_{T,j}}(p)^*\Pi_{j,k}^{\lambda,M}(p)
      \widehat{A_{T,k}}(p), \\
    \Pi_{j,k}^{\lambda,M}(p)
    &\coloneq \sum_{\substack{q\in 2\pi\mathbb Z^2\\|q|\leqslant M}}
      \frac{1}{(1+\lambda+|q|^2)^2}
      \left(\delta_{j,k}
      -\frac{(2q+p)_j(2q+p)_k}{1+\lambda+|q+p|^2}\right).
  \end{align*}
  Applying \eqref{eq:decomp_scq} with $\mathbb{A}=\mathbb{A}_T$ and $B=0$, and taking the trace after projection by $P_M$, gives the following identity. The first-order term vanishes by symmetry, as in \eqref{eq:tr_q1_vanishes}.
  \begin{align}\label{eq:projected-decomposition}
    &\operatorname{Tr} P_M\bigl((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1}
      -(H_{A,T}+\lambda)^{-1}\bigr)P_M \nonumber\\
    &\quad=(\lambda_{A_T,T}-1-{\mathrm{c}}_T)
      \operatorname{Tr} P_M(L_0+1+\lambda)^{-2}P_M
      +\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\lambda,M}(A_T,A_T) \nonumber\\
    &\qquad+\operatorname{Tr} P_M{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}(\lambda)P_M.
  \end{align}
  Now set,
  \begin{align*}
    \mathcal{Q}_{T,M}^{\mathrm{Gal}}(A_T)
    \coloneq {}&-\frac{\lambda_{A_T,T}-1}{2}\bar p_M+{\mathrm{o}}_{T,M}\\
      &+\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr} P_M
      \bigl((L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1}
      -(H_{A,T}+\lambda)^{-1}\bigr)P_M\,\mathrm{d}\lambda,
  \end{align*}
  then \eqref{eq:projected-decomposition} implies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:Gal-Q-decomposition}
    \mathcal{Q}_{T,M}^{\mathrm{Gal}}(A_T)
    =\int_0^\infty\bigl(\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\lambda,M}(A_T,A_T)
      -\mathbb{E}^\Theta\mathbb{E}^{\mathrm{A}}[\boldsymbol{\Pi}^\lambda(A_T,A_T)]\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
      +\int_0^\infty
        \operatorname{Tr} P_M{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}(\lambda)P_M\,\mathrm{d}\lambda.
  \end{equation}
  Now for fixed $T$ it follows from Lemma \ref{lemma:8pi} below, that
  \[\int_{0}^{\infty} \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\lambda,M}(A_T,A_T) \mathrm{d} \lambda \to \int_0^{\infty}\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\lambda} (A_T,A_T)\mathrm{d}\lambda+\frac{1}{4\pi}\|A_{T}\|^2_{L^2}\]
  Furthermore  $
    \left|\operatorname{Tr} P_M{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}(\lambda)P_M\right|
    \leqslant\operatorname{Tr}\left|{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}(\lambda)\right|,$  and the right-hand side is integrable in $\lambda$. These two facts together with dominated convergence  therefore yield
  \begin{align*}
    \mathcal{Q}_{T,M}^{\mathrm{Gal}}(A_T)-\frac{1}{4\pi}\|A_{T}\|^2_{L^2}
      \longrightarrow&\int_0^\infty \mathbb{V}_{A_T}(\lambda) \,\mathrm{d}\lambda
      +\int_0^\infty
        \operatorname{Tr}{\mathrm{Rem}}_{\mathbb{A}_T,0}(\lambda)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\\
      =&\mathcal{Q}_\infty(\mathbf{A}_T,0).
 \end{align*}

  Finally, \eqref{eq:compressed-resolvents} shows that the logarithm of the
  expression on the right-hand side of the lemma equals
  \begin{align*}
    &\frac{\lambda_{A_T,T}-1}{2}\bar p_M-{\mathrm{o}}_{T,M} \\
    &\quad+\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr} P_M\bigl((H_{A,T}+\lambda)^{-1}
      -(L_0+1+\lambda)^{-1}\bigr)P_M\,\mathrm{d}\lambda+\frac{1}{4\pi}\|A_T\|^2_{L^2}+o_M(1),
  \end{align*}
  which is $-\mathcal{Q}_{T,M}^{\mathrm{Gal}}(A_T)+\frac{1}{4\pi}\|A_T\|^2_{L^2}+o_M(1)$ and therefore converges to $-\mathcal{Q}_\infty(\mathbf{A}_T,0)$.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem:compressed-elliptic}
  For every $f\in QL^2$, uniformly in $M$ and $\lambda\geqslant0$,
  \begin{align*}
    \|(-\Delta+\lambda+1)(G_{QQ}+\lambda)^{-1}f\|_{L^2}
      &\leqslant C(A_T)\|f\|_{L^2}, \\
    \|(1-\Delta)G_{QQ}^{-1}f\|_{L^2}
      &\leqslant C(A_T)\|f\|_{L^2}.
  \end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lemma:8pi}
  For fixed smooth $A_T$, we have
  \[ \lim_{M \rightarrow \infty} \int^{\infty}_0 \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\lambda , M} (A_T,
